items.statement: Every non-edgeless finite tree has at least two leaf nodes.

items.title: Finite Union of Finite Sets is Finite
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set of finite sets.
Then the union of $S$ is finite.

items.title: Finitely Satisfiable Theory has Maximal Finitely Satisfiable Extension
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a finitely satisfiable $\LL$-theory.
Then there exists a finitely satisfiable $\LL$-theory $T'$ which contains $T$ as a subset such that:
:for all $\LL$-sentences $\phi$, either $\phi \in T'$ or $\neg \phi \in T'$.

items.title: First-Order Reaction
items.statement:
Let a substance decompose spontaneously in a '''first-order reaction'''.
Let $x_0$ be a measure of the quantity of that substance at time $t = 0$.
Let the quantity of the substance that remains after time $t$ be $x$.
Then:
:$x = x_0 e^{-k t}$
where $k$ is the rate constant.

items.title: First Element of Geometric Sequence not dividing Second
items.statement:
Let $P = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence of integers of length $n$.
Let $a_0$ not be a divisor of $a_1$.
Then:
:$\forall j, k \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, n}, j \ne k: a_j \nmid a_k$
That is, if the initial term of $P$ does not divide the second, no term of $P$ divides any other term of $P$.
{{:Euclid:Proposition/VIII/6}}

items.title: First Order ODE/(x + y) dx = (x - y) dy
items.statement:
is a homogeneous differential equation with general solution:
:$\arctan \dfrac y x = \ln \sqrt {x^2 + y^2} + C$

items.title: First Order ODE/dy = k y dx
items.statement:
Let $k \in \R$ be a real number.
The first order ODE:
:$\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = k y$
has the general solution:
:$y = C e^{k x}$

items.title: First Order ODE/x dy = (y + x^2 + 9 y^2) dx
items.statement:
The first order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x \rd y = \paren {y + x^2 + 9 y^2} \rd x$
has the general solution:
:$\map \arctan {\dfrac {3 y} x} = 3 x + C$

items.title: First Order ODE/x y dy = x^2 dy + y^2 dx
items.statement:
The first order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x y \rd y = x^2 \rd y + y^2 \rd x$
has the general solution:
:$y = x \ln y + C x$

items.title: First Order ODE/y dx + (x^2 y - x) dy = 0
items.statement:
The first order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y \rd x + \paren {x^2 y - x} \rd y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$\dfrac {y^2} 2 - \dfrac y x = C$

items.title: First Sylow Theorem
items.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number.
Let $G$ be a group such that:
:$\order G = k p^n$
where:
:$\order G$ denotes the order of $G$
:$p$ is not a divisor of $k$.
Then $G$ has at least one Sylow $p$-subgroup.

items.title: First Translation Property of Laplace Transforms
items.statement:
:$\laptrans {e^{a t} \map f t} = \map F {s - a}$
everywhere that $\laptrans f$ exists, for $\map \Re s > a$

items.title: Five Platonic Solids
Fixed Point of Progressing Mapping on Minimally Inductive Class is Greatest Element
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$.
Let $x$ be a fixed point of $g$.
Then $x$ is the greatest element of $M$.

items.title: Floor of x+m over n
items.statement:
Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$.
Let $x \in \R$.
Then:
:$\floor {\dfrac {x + m} n} = \floor {\dfrac {\floor x + m} n}$
where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

items.title: Floquet's Theorem
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf A \left({t}\right)$ be a continuous matrix function with period $T$.
Let $\Phi \left({t}\right)$ be a fundamental matrix of the Floquet system $\mathbf x' = \mathbf A \left({t}\right) \mathbf x$.
Then $\Phi \left({t + T}\right)$ is also a fundamental matrix.
Moreover, there exists:
: A nonsingular, continuously differentiable matrix function $\mathbf P \left({t}\right)$ with period $T$
: A constant (possibly complex) matrix $\mathbf B$ such that:
::$\Phi \left({t}\right) = \mathbf P \left({t}\right) e^{\mathbf Bt}$

items.title: Formulation 1 Rank Axioms Implies Rank Function of Matroid
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set.
Let $\rho : \powerset S \to \Z$ be a mapping from the power set of $S$ to the integers.
Let $\rho$ satisfy formulation 1 of the rank axioms:
{{:Axiom:Rank Axioms (Matroid)/Definition 1}}
Then $\rho$ is the rank function of a matroid on $S$.

items.title: Formulation 1 Rank Axioms Implies Rank Function of Matroid/Lemma 5
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set.
Let $\rho : \powerset S \to \Z$ be a mapping from the power set of $S$ to the integers.
Let $\rho$ satisfy formulation 1 of the rank axioms:
{{:Axiom:Rank Axioms (Matroid)/Definition 1}}
Let $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ where:
:$\mathscr I = \set{X \subseteq S : \map \rho X = \card X}$
Then $M$ satisfies matroid axiom $(\text I 2)$.

items.title: Fort Space is Scattered
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on an infinite set $S$.
Then $T$ is a scattered space.

items.title: Fourier Series/Absolute Value of x over Minus Pi to Pi
items.statement:
For $x \in \openint {-\pi} \pi$:
:$\ds \size x = \frac \pi 2 - \frac 4 \pi \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\map \cos {2 n - 1} x} {\paren {2 n - 1}^2}$

items.title: Fourier Series/Identity Function over Minus Pi to Pi
items.statement:
For $x \in \openint {-\pi} \pi$:
:$\ds x = 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n + 1} } n \sin n x$

items.title: Fourier Series for Logarithm of Sine of x over 0 to Pi
items.statement:
:$\ds \map \ln {\sin x} = -\ln 2 - \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\cos 2 n x} n$
where $0 < x < \pi$.

items.title: Fully Normal Space is Paracompact
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a fully normal space.
Then $T$ is paracompact.

items.title: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
items.statement:
Every non-constant polynomial with coefficients in $\C$ has a root in $\C$.
That is, the field of complex numbers is algebraically closed.

items.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus/First Part
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Let $F$ be a real function which is defined on $\closedint a b$ by:
:$\ds \map F x = \int_a^x \map f t \rd t$
Then $F$ is a primitive of $f$ on $\closedint a b$.

items.title: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus/Second Part
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Then:
:$(1): \quad f$ has a primitive on $\closedint a b$
:$(2): \quad$ If $F$ is any primitive of $f$ on $\closedint a b$, then:
:::$\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t = \map F b - \map F a = \bigintlimits {\map F t} a b$

items.title: GM-HM Inequality
items.statement:
Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{> 0}$ be strictly positive real numbers.
Let $G_n$ be the geometric mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.
Let $H_n$ be the harmonic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.
Then:
:$G_n \ge H_n$

items.title: Gamma Difference Equation
items.statement: :$\map \Gamma {z + 1} = z \, \map \Gamma z$

items.title: Gamma Function of One Half
items.statement: :$\map \Gamma {\dfrac 1 2} = \sqrt \pi$

items.title: Gauss's Hypergeometric Theorem
items.statement: :$\map F {a, b; c; 1} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma c \map \Gamma {c - a - b} } {\map \Gamma {c - a} \map \Gamma {c - b} }$

items.title: Gauss's Lemma on Primitive Rational Polynomials
items.statement:
Let $\Q$ be the field of rational numbers.
Let $\Q \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials over $\Q$ in one indeterminate $X$.
Let $\map f X, \map g X \in \Q \sqbrk X$ be primitive polynomials.
Then their product $f g$ is also a primitive polynomial.

items.title: Gauss-Ostrogradsky Theorem
items.statement:
Let $U$ be a subset of $\R^3$ which is compact and has a piecewise smooth boundary $\partial U$.
Let $\mathbf V: \R^3 \to \R^3$ be a smooth vector field defined on a neighborhood of $U$.
Then:
:$\ds \iiint \limits_U \paren {\nabla \cdot \mathbf V} \rd v = \iint \limits_{\partial U} \mathbf V \cdot \mathbf n \rd S$
where $\mathbf n$ is the unit normal to $\partial U$, directed outwards.
That is, the sum of all expansions of $\mathbf V$ within $U$ equals the flux of $\mathbf V$ across the boundary of $U$.

items.title: Gaussian Delta Sequence
items.statement:
thumb500pxThe graph of the Gaussian delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the graph becomes thinner and taller. The area of under each Gaussian is equal to $1$.
Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a sequence such that:
:$\map {\delta_n} x := \dfrac n {\sqrt \pi} e^{- n^2 x^2}$
Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a delta sequence.
That is, in the distributional sense it holds that:
:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {\delta_n} x = \map \delta x$
or
:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map {\delta_n} x \map \phi x \rd x = \map \delta \phi$
where:
:$\phi \in \map \DD \R$ is a test function
:$\delta$ is the Dirac delta distribution
:$\map \delta x$ is the abuse of notation, usually interpreted as an infinitely thin and tall spike with its area equal to $1$.

items.title: Gaussian Integers form Euclidean Domain
items.statement:
Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ be the integral domain of Gaussian Integers.
Let $\nu: \Z \sqbrk i \to \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: 
:$\forall a \in \Z \sqbrk i: \map \nu a = \cmod a^2$ 
where $\cmod a$ is the (complex) modulus of $a$.
Then $\nu$ is a Euclidean valuation on $\Z \sqbrk i$.
Hence $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ with $\nu: \Z \sqbrk i \to \Z$ forms a Euclidean domain.

items.title: General Associative Law for Ordinal Sum
items.statement:
Let $x$ be a finite ordinal.
Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{x + 1} a_i = a_1 + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^x a_{i + 1}$

items.title: General Associativity Theorem
items.statement: If an operation is associative on $3$ entities, then it is associative on any number of them.

items.title: General Associativity Theorem/Formulation 2
items.statement:
Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ and let $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ be elements of a set $S$.
Let $\circ$ be an associative operation on $S$.
Let the set $\map {P_n} {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n}$ be defined inductively by:
:$\map {P_1} {a_1} = \set {a_1}$
:$\map {P_2} {a_1, a_2} = \set {a_1 \circ a_2}$
:$\map {P_n} {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n} = \set {x \circ y: x \in \map {P_r} {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_r} \land y \in \map {P_s} {a_{r + 1}, a_{r + 2}, \ldots, a_{r + s} }, n = r + s}$
Then $\map {P_n} {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n}$ consists of a unique entity which we can denote $a_1 \circ a_2 \circ \ldots \circ a_n$.

items.title: General Solution to Chebyshev's Differential Equation
items.statement:
Consider '''Chebyshev's differential equation''':
:$(1): \quad \ds \paren {1 - x^2} \frac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} - x \frac {\d y} {\d x} + n^2 y = 0$
where $n \in \N$.
The general solution to $(1)$ is given by:
:$y = \begin {cases} A \map {T_n} x + B \sqrt {1 - x^2} \, \map {U_{n - 1} } x + C \map \cos {n \arcsin x} + D \map \sin {n \arcsin x} & : n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots \\ \\ A \arccos x + B \arcsin x + C & : n = 0 \end {cases}$
where:
:$\map {T_n} x$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of order $n$
:$\map {U_n} x$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind of order $n$
:$\size x < 1$

items.title: Generating Function for Elementary Symmetric Function
Geometric Sequence in Lowest Terms has Coprime Extremes
items.statement:
A geometric sequence of integers in lowest terms has extremes which are coprime.
{{:Euclid:Proposition/VIII/3}}

items.title: Geometric Sequence with Coprime Extremes is in Lowest Terms
items.statement:
Let $G_n = \sequence {a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n}$ be a geometric sequence of integers.
Let:
:$a_0 \perp a_n$
where $\perp$ denotes coprimality.
Then $G_n$ is in its lowest terms.

items.title: Graph Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
items.statement: Graph isomorphism is an equivalence relation.

items.title: Grassmann's Identity
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a division ring.
Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_K$ be a $K$-vector space.
Let $M$ and $N$ be finite-dimensional subspaces of $G$.
Then the sum $M + N$ and intersection $M \cap N$ are finite-dimensional, and:
:$\map \dim {M + N} + \map \dim {M \cap N} = \map \dim M + \map \dim N$

items.title: Greatest Lower Bound Property
items.statement:
Let $S \subset \R$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers such that $S$ is bounded below.
Then $S$ admits an infimum in $\R$.
This is known as the '''greatest lower bound property''' of the real numbers.

items.title: Group/Examples/x+y over 1+xy
items.statement:
Let $G = \set {x \in \R: -1 < x < 1}$ be the set of all real numbers whose absolute value is less than $1$.
Let $\circ: G \times G \to \R$ be the binary operation defined as:
:$\forall x, y \in G: x \circ y = \dfrac {x + y} {1 + x y}$
The algebraic structure $\struct {G, \circ}$ is a group.

items.title: Group/Examples/x+y over 1+xy/Isomorphic to Real Numbers
items.statement: $\struct {G, \circ}$ is isomorphic to the additive group of real numbers $\struct {\R, +}$.

items.title: Group Epimorphism is Isomorphism iff Kernel is Trivial
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ and $\struct {H, \odot}$ be groups.
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \oplus} \to \struct {H, \odot}$ be a group epimorphism.
Let $e_G$ and $e_H$ be the identities of $G$ and $H$ respectively.
Let $K = \map \ker \phi$ be the kernel of $\phi$.
Then:
:the epimorphism $\phi$ is an isomorphism
{{iff}}
:$K = \set {e_G}$

items.title: Group Homomorphism Preserves Identity
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups.
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group homomorphism.
Let:
:$e_G$ be the identity of $G$
:$e_H$ be the identity of $H$.
Then:
:$\map \phi {e_G} = e_H$

items.title: Group Homomorphism Preserves Inverses
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups.
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to\struct {H, *}$ be a group homomorphism.
Let:
:$e_G$ be the identity of $G$
:$e_H$ be the identity of $H$
Then:
:$\forall x \in G: \map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$

items.title: Group Isomorphism Preserves Identity
items.statement:
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group isomorphism.
Let:
:$e_G$ be the identity of $\struct {G, \circ}$
:$e_H$ be the identity of $\struct {H, *}$.
Then:
:$\map \phi {e_G} = e_H$

items.title: Group Isomorphism Preserves Inverses
items.statement:
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group isomorphism.
Let:
:$e_G$ be the identity of $\struct {G, \circ}$
:$e_H$ be the identity of $\struct {H, *}$.
Then:
: $\forall g \in G: \map \phi {g^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi g}^{-1}$

items.title: Group Product Identity therefore Inverses
items.statement:
Let $g$ and $h$ be elements of a group $G$ whose identity element is $e$.
Then if either:
:$g h = e$
or:
:$h g = e$
it follows that:
:$g = h^{-1}$
and:
:$h = g^{-1}$

items.title: Group Product Identity therefore Inverses/Part 1
items.statement: :$g h = e \implies h = g^{-1}$ and $g = h^{-1}$

items.title: Group Product Identity therefore Inverses/Part 2
items.statement: :$h g = e \implies h = g^{-1}$ and $g = h^{-1}$

items.title: Group does not Necessarily have Subgroup of Order of Divisor of its Order
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is $n$.
Let $d$ be a divisor of $n$.
Then it is not necessarily the case that $G$ has a subgroup of order $d$.

items.title: Group has Latin Square Property
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Then $G$ satisfies the Latin square property.
That is, for all $a, b \in G$, there exists a unique $g \in G$ such that $a \circ g = b$.
Similarly, there exists a unique $h \in G$ such that $h \circ a = b$.

items.title: Group of Order 15 is Cyclic Group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a group whose order is $15$.
Then $G$ is cyclic.

items.title: Group of Order 35 is Cyclic Group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a group whose order is $35$.
Then $G$ is cyclic.

items.title: Group of Order p q is Cyclic
items.statement:
Let $p, q$ be primes such that $p < q$ and $p$ does not divide $q - 1$.
Let $G$ be a group of order $p q$.
Then $G$ is cyclic.

items.title: Half-Range Fourier Cosine Series/Identity Function/0 to Pi
Half Angle Formula for Tangent/Corollary 2
items.statement: :$\tan \dfrac \theta 2 = \dfrac {1 - \cos \theta} {\sin \theta}$

items.title: Half Angle Formulas/Cosine
Half Angle Formulas/Sine
Harmonic Number is not Integer
items.statement:
Let $H_n$ be the $n$th harmonic number.
Then $H_n$ is not an integer for $n \ge 2$.
That is, the only harmonic numbers that are integers are $H_0$ and $H_1$.

items.title: Harmonic Series is Divergent
items.statement:
The harmonic series:
:$\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 n$ 
diverges.

items.title: Hartogs' Lemma (Set Theory)
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Then there exists an ordinal $\alpha$ such that there is no injection from $\alpha$ to $S$.

items.title: Hausdorff's Maximal Principle implies Kuratowski's Lemma
items.statement:
Let Hausdorff's Maximal Principle be accepted as true.
Then Kuratowski's Lemma holds.

items.title: Hausdorff Paradox
items.statement: There exists a disjoint decomposition of the sphere $\mathbb S^2$ into four sets $A, B, C, Q$ such that $A, B, C, B \cup C$ are all congruent and $Q$ is countable.

items.title: Heine-Borel Theorem/Euclidean Space
items.statement:
Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$.
Let $C$ be a subspace of the Euclidean space $\R^n$.
Then $C$ is closed and bounded {{iff}} it is compact.

items.title: Heine-Cantor Theorem
items.statement:
Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces.
Let $M_1$ be compact.
Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a continuous mapping.
Then $f$ is uniformly continuous.

items.title: Hellinger-Toeplitz Theorem
items.statement:
Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space.
Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a Hermitian operator.
That is: 
:$\innerprod {T x} y = \innerprod x {T y}$ for each $x, y \in \HH$.
Then: 
:$T$ is bounded.

items.title: Hermitian Matrix has Real Eigenvalues
items.statement: Every Hermitian matrix has eigenvalues which are all real numbers.

items.title: Hermitian Operator has Orthogonal Eigenvectors
items.statement: The eigenvectors of a Hermitian operator are orthogonal.

items.title: Hero's Method
items.statement:
Let $a \in \R$ be a real number such that $a > 0$.
Let $x_1 \in \R$ be a real number such that $x_1 > 0$.
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined recursively by:
:$\forall n \in \N_{>0}: x_{n + 1} = \dfrac {x_n + \dfrac a {x_n} } 2$
Then $x_n \to \sqrt a$ as $n \to \infty$.

items.title: Heron's Formula
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with sides $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively.
Then the area $\AA$ of $\triangle ABC$ is given by:
:$\AA = \sqrt {s \paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} \paren {s - c} }$
where $s = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$ is the semiperimeter of $\triangle ABC$.

items.title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Metric Space
items.statement:
Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent.
Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$.
Then $\ell^2$ is a metric space.

items.title: Honsberger's Identity
items.statement: :$\forall m, n \in \Z_{>0}: F_{m + n} = F_{m - 1} F_n + F_m F_{n + 1}$

items.title: Hyperbolic Cosine Function is Even
items.statement: :$\map \cosh {-x} = \cosh x$

items.title: Hyperbolic Cosine of Complex Number
items.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers.
Let $i$ be the imaginary unit.
Then:
:$\map \cosh {a + b i} = \cosh a \cos b + i \sinh a \sin b$
where:
:$\cos$ denotes the real cosine function
:$\sin$ denotes the real sine function
:$\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function
:$\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

items.title: Hyperbolic Secant Function is Even
items.statement: :$\map \sech {-x} = \sech x$

items.title: Hyperbolic Sine Function is Odd
items.statement: :$\map \sinh {-x} = -\sinh x$

items.title: Hypothetical Syllogism
Hypothetical Syllogism/Formulation 3
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \land \paren {q \implies r} } \implies \paren {p \implies r}$

items.title: Hypothetical Syllogism/Formulation 4
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {\paren {q \implies r} \implies \paren {p \implies r} }$

items.title: Hypothetical Syllogism/Formulation 5
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {q \implies r} \implies \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r} }$

items.title: Idempotent Elements form Subsemigroup of Commutative Semigroup
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup such that $\circ$ is commutative.
Let $I$ be the set of all elements of $S$ that are idempotent under $\circ$.
That is:
:$I = \set {x \in S: x \circ x = x}$
Then $\struct {I, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

items.title: Identity Mapping is Left Identity
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then:
:$I_T \circ f = f$
where $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

items.title: Identity Mapping is Order Isomorphism
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set.
The identity mapping $I_S$ is an order isomorphism from $\struct {S, \preceq}$ to itself.

items.title: Identity Mapping is Right Identity
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then:
:$f \circ I_S = f$
where $I_S$ is the identity mapping on $S$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

items.title: Identity is Unique
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure that has an identity element $e \in S$.
Then $e$ is unique.

items.title: Identity is only Idempotent Element in Group
items.statement: Every group has exactly one idempotent element: the identity.

items.title: Identity of Group Direct Product
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of the two groups $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$.
Let $e_G$ be the identity for $\struct {G, \circ_1}$.
Let $e_H$ be the identity for $\struct {H, \circ_2}$.
Then $\tuple {e_G, e_H}$ is the identity for $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$.

items.title: Identity of Group is Unique
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which has an identity element $e \in G$.
Then $e$ is unique.

items.title: Image of Convergent Sequence in Topological Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space. 
Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence with $x_n \to x$. 
Let: 
:$E = \set {x_n : n \in \N}$
Then $E$ is von Neumann-bounded.

items.title: Image of Intersection under Injection
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then:
:$\forall A, B \subseteq S: f \sqbrk {A \cap B} = f \sqbrk A \cap f \sqbrk B$
{{iff}} $f$ is an injection.
This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as:
:$\forall A, B \subseteq S: \map {f^\to} {A \cap B} = \map {f^\to} A \cap \map {f^\to} B$

items.title: Image of Intersection under Mapping
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$.
Then:
:$f \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq f \sqbrk {S_1} \cap f \sqbrk {S_2}$
This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as:
:$\forall S_1, S_2 \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq \map {f^\to} {S_1} \cap \map {f^\to} {S_2}$

items.title: Image of Real Interval under Continuous Real Function is Real Interval
items.statement:
Let $I$ be a real interval.
Let $f: I \to \R$ be a continuous real function.
Then the image of $f$ is a real interval.

items.title: Image of Set Difference under Mapping
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
The set difference of the images of two subsets of $S$ is a subset of the image of the set difference.
That is:
Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$.
Then:
:$f \sqbrk {S_1} \setminus f \sqbrk {S_2} \subseteq f \sqbrk {S_1 \setminus S_2}$
where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

items.title: Image of Ultrafilter is Ultrafilter
items.statement:
Let $X, Y$ be sets.
Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping.
Let $\FF$ be an ultrafilter on $X$.
Then the image filter $f \sqbrk \FF$ is an ultrafilter on $Y$.

items.title: Image of Union under Mapping
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$.
Then:
:$f \sqbrk {A \cup B} = f \sqbrk A \cup f \sqbrk B$
This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as:
:$\forall A, B \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {A \cup B} = \map {f^\to} A \cup \map {f^\to} B$

items.title: Increasing Sum of Binomial Coefficients
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n j \binom n j = n 2^{n - 1}$

items.title: Indirect Proof
items.statement:
Let $P$ be a proposition whose truth value is to be proved (either true or false).
An '''indirect proof''' has one of the following two argument forms:
=== Reductio ad Absurdum ===
A '''reductio ad absurdum''' argument for the truth of $P$ is a valid argument which takes as a premise the negation of $P$, and from it deduces a contradiction:
{{:Reductio ad Absurdum/Proof Rule}}
=== Proof by Contradiction ===
A '''proof by contradiction''' argument for the falsehood of $P$ is a valid argument which takes $P$ as a premise, and from it directly deduces a contradiction:
{{:Proof by Contradiction/Proof Rule}}

items.title: Inequality Rule for Real Sequences
Infinite Sequence Property of Strictly Well-Founded Relation
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure.
Then $\RR$ is a strictly well-founded relation {{iff}} there is no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that:
:$\forall n \in \N: a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n$

items.title: Infinite Sequence Property of Strictly Well-Founded Relation/Reverse Implication
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure.
Let $\RR$ be such that there exists no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that:
:$\forall n \in \N: a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n$
Then $\RR$ is a strictly well-founded relation.

items.title: Infinite Sequence Property of Well-Founded Relation
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure.
Then $\RR$ is a well-founded relation {{iff}} there exists no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that:
:$\forall n \in \N: \paren {a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n} \text { and } \paren {a_{n + 1} \ne a_n}$

items.title: Infinite Sequence Property of Well-Founded Relation/Reverse Implication
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure.
Let $\RR$ be such that there exists no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that:
:$\forall n \in \N: \paren {a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n} \text { and } \paren {a_{n + 1} \ne a_n}$
Then $\RR$ is a well-founded relation.

items.title: Infinite Set has Countably Infinite Subset
items.statement: Every infinite set has a countably infinite subset.

items.title: Infinite Set is Equivalent to Proper Subset
items.statement: A set is infinite {{iff}} it is equivalent to one of its proper subsets.

items.title: Injection has Surjective Left Inverse Mapping
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \ne \O$.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a injection.
Then there exists a surjection $g: T \to S$ such that:
:$g \circ f = I_S$

items.title: Injection iff Left Inverse
items.statement:
A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is an injection {{iff}}:
:$\exists g: T \to S: g \circ f = I_S$
where $g$ is a mapping.
That is, {{iff}} $f$ has a left inverse.

items.title: Inscribed Angle Theorem
items.statement:
An inscribed angle is equal to half the angle that is subtended by that arc.
:300px
Thus, in the figure above:
:$\angle ABC = \frac 1 2 \angle ADC$
{{EuclidSaid}}
:''In a circle the angle at the center is double of the angle at the circumference, when the angles have the same circumference as base.''
{{EuclidPropRef|III|20}}

items.title: Integer Addition is Associative
items.statement:
The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is associative:
:$\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x + \paren {y + z} = \paren {x + y} + z$

items.title: Integer Addition is Commutative
items.statement:
The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is commutative:
:$\forall x, y \in \Z: x + y = y + x$

items.title: Integer Combination of Coprime Integers
items.statement:
Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers, not both zero.
Then:
:$a$ and $b$ are coprime
{{iff}}:
:there exists an integer combination of them equal to $1$:
::$\forall a, b \in \Z: a \perp b \iff \exists m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = 1$
In such an integer combination $m a + n b = 1$, the integers $m$ and $n$ are also coprime.

items.title: Integer Combination of Coprime Integers/Necessary Condition
items.statement:
Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers, not both zero.
Let $a$ and $b$ be such that there exists an integer combination of them equal to $1$.
Then $a$ and $b$ are coprime:
:$\forall a, b \in \Z: \exists m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = 1 \implies a \perp b$
In such an integer combination $m a + n b = 1$, the integers $m$ and $n$ are also coprime.

items.title: Integer Combination of Coprime Integers/Sufficient Condition
items.statement:
Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers, not both zero.
Let $a$ and $b$ be coprime to each other.
Then there exists an integer combination of them equal to $1$:
:$\forall a, b \in \Z: a \perp b \implies \exists m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = 1$

items.title: Integer Coprime to Factors is Coprime to Whole
items.statement:
Let $a, b, c \in \Z$ be integers.
Let:
:$a \perp b$
:$a \perp c$
where $\perp$ denotes coprimality.
Then:
:$a \perp b c$

items.title: Integer Divisor Results
items.statement:
Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers.
Let $m \divides n$ denote that $m$ is a divisor of $n$.
The following results all hold:

items.title: Integer Divisor Results/Integer Divides Itself
items.statement: :$n \divides n$

items.title: Integer is Expressible as Product of Primes
items.statement:
Let $n$ be an integer such that $n > 1$.
Then $n$ can be expressed as the product of one or more primes.

items.title: Integers form Ordered Integral Domain
items.statement: The integers $\Z$ form an ordered integral domain under addition and multiplication.

items.title: Integral of Constant
items.statement: Let $c$ be a constant.

items.title: Integral of Power
items.statement: :$\ds \forall n \in \R_{\ne -1}: \int_0^b x^n \rd x = \frac {b^{n + 1} } {n + 1}$

items.title: Integral of Reciprocal is Divergent/Unbounded Above
items.statement: :$\ds \int_1^n \frac {\d x} x \to +\infty$ as $n \to + \infty$

items.title: Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -t^2
items.statement: :$\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-t^2} \rd t = \dfrac {\sqrt \pi} 2$

items.title: Integral to Infinity of Sine p x over x
items.statement: :$\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin p x} x \rd x = \begin {cases} \dfrac \pi 2 & : p > 0 \\ \\ 0 & : p = 0 \\ \\ -\dfrac \pi 2 & : p < 0 \end {cases}$

items.title: Integral with respect to Dirac Measure
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space.
Let $x \in X$, and let $\delta_x$ be the Dirac measure at $x$.
Let $f \in \MM _{\overline \R}, f: X \to \overline \R$ be a measurable function.
Then:
:$\ds \int f \rd \delta_x = \map f x$
where the integral sign denotes the $\delta_x$-integral.

items.title: Integration by Parts
items.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Let $f$ and $g$ have primitives $F$ and $G$ respectively on $\closedint a b$.
Then:
=== Primitive ===
{{:Integration by Parts/Primitive}}
=== Definite Integral ===
{{:Integration by Parts/Definite Integral}}
This technique is called '''integration by parts'''.

items.title: Integration by Parts/Primitive
items.statement:
:$\ds \int \map f t \map G t \rd t = \map F t \map G t - \int \map F t \map g t \rd t$
on $\closedint a b$.

items.title: Interior Extremum Theorem
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$.
Let $f$ have a local minimum or local maximum at $\xi \in \openint a b$.
Then:
:$\map {f'} \xi = 0$

items.title: Interior may not equal Exterior of Exterior
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of the underlying set $S$ of $T$.
Let $A^e$ be the  exterior of $A$.
Let $A^\circ$ be the  interior of $A$.
Then it is not necessarily the case that:
:$A^{ee} = A^\circ$

items.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
items.statement:
Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval.
Let $f: I \to \R$ be continuous on $I$.
Then $f$ is a Darboux function.
That is:
Let $a, b \in I$.
Let $k \in \R$ lie between $\map f a$ and $\map f b$.
That is, either:
:$\map f a < k < \map f b$
or:
:$\map f b < k < \map f a$
Then $\exists c \in \openint a b$ such that $\map f c = k$.

items.title: Internal Direct Product Theorem/General Result
Internal Group Direct Product Commutativity
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$.
Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$.
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be the internal group direct product of $H$ and $K$.
Then:
:$\forall h \in H, k \in K: h \circ k = k \circ h$

items.title: Intersecting Chords Theorem
items.statement:
Let $AC$ and $BD$ both be chords of the same circle.
Let $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$.
Then $AE \cdot EC = DE \cdot EB$.

items.title: Intersection is Associative
items.statement:
Set intersection is associative:
:$A \cap \paren {B \cap C} = \paren {A \cap B} \cap C$

items.title: Intersection is Associative/Family of Sets
items.statement:
Let $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ and $\family {I_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be indexed families of sets.
Let $\ds I = \bigcap_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} I_\lambda$.
Then:
:$\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} S_i = \bigcap_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} \paren {\bigcap_{i \mathop \in I_\lambda} S_i}$

items.title: Intersection is Commutative
items.statement:
Set intersection is commutative:
:$S \cap T = T \cap S$

items.title: Intersection is Commutative/Family of Sets
items.statement:
Let $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of sets.
Let $\ds I = \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ denote the intersection of $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$.
Let $J \subseteq I$ be a subset of $I$.
Then:
:$\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} S_i = \bigcap_{j \mathop \in J} S_j \cap \bigcap_{k \mathop \in \relcomp I J} S_k = \bigcap_{k \mathop \in \relcomp I J} S_k \cap \bigcap_{j \mathop \in J} S_j$
where $\relcomp I J$ denotes the complement of $J$ relative to $I$.

items.title: Intersection of Closed Set with Compact Subspace is Compact
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $H \subseteq S$ be closed in $T$.
Let $K \subseteq S$ be compact in $T$.
Then $H \cap K$ is compact in $T$.

items.title: Intersection of Non-Empty Class is Set
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a non-empty class.
Let $\bigcap A$ denote the intersection of $A$.
Then $\bigcap A$ is a set.

items.title: Intersection of Subsemigroups
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup.
Let $\struct {T_1, \circ}$ and $\struct {T_2, \circ}$ be subsemigroups of $\struct {S, \circ}$.
Then the intersection of $\struct {T_1, \circ}$ and $\struct {T_2, \circ}$ is itself a subsemigroup of that $\struct {S, \circ}$.

items.title: Intersection of Subsemigroups/General Result
items.statement:
Let $\mathbb H$ be a set of subsemigroups of $\struct {S, \circ}$, where $\mathbb H \ne \O$.
Then the intersection $\bigcap \mathbb H$ of the members of $\mathbb H$ is the largest subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$ contained in each member of $\mathbb H$.

items.title: Intersection with Set Difference is Set Difference with Intersection
items.statement: : $\left({R \setminus S}\right) \cap T = \left({R \cap T}\right) \setminus S$

items.title: Intersection with Subset is Subset
items.statement: :$S \subseteq T \iff S \cap T = S$

items.title: Interval of Totally Ordered Set is Order-Convex
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set.
Let $I \subseteq S$ be an interval in $S$.
Then $I$ is order-convex.

items.title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent is Odd Function
Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent is Odd Function
Inverse Mapping is Unique
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
If $f$ has an inverse mapping, then that inverse mapping is unique.
That is, if:
:$f$ and $g$ are inverse mappings of each other
and
:$f$ and $h$ are inverse mappings of each other
then $g = h$.

items.title: Inverse Tangent of Imaginary Number
items.statement: :$\map {\tan^{-1} } {i x} = i \tanh^{-1} x$

items.title: Inverse in Group is Unique
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Then every element $x \in G$ has exactly one inverse:
:$\forall x \in G: \exists_1 x^{-1} \in G: x \circ x^{-1} = e^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ x$
where $e$ is the identity element of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

items.title: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Injection
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping.
Then $f$ is an injection.

items.title: Inverse of Circle Not Through Inversion Center
items.statement:
Let $\CC$ be a circle in the plane on center $O$.
Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $\CC$ as the inversion circle. 
Then $O$ is the inversion center.
Let $K$ be an arbitrary circle distinct from $\CC$ and not through $O$.
Then the image under $T$ of all the points on $K$ lie on the same circle, distinct from both $K$ and $\CC$.

items.title: Inverse of Composite Bijection
items.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be bijections such that $\Dom g = \Cdm f$.
Then:
:$\paren {g \circ f}^{-1} = f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}$
and $f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}$ is itself a bijection.

items.title: Inverse of Field Product
items.statement:
Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$.
Let $a, b \in F$ such that $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$.
Then:
:$\paren {a \times b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \times a^{-1}$

items.title: Inverse of Generator of Cyclic Group is Generator
items.statement:
Let $\gen g = G$ be a cyclic group.
Then:
:$G = \gen {g^{-1} }$
where $g^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $g$.
Thus, in general, a generator of a cyclic group is not unique.

items.title: Inverse of Group Inverse
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $g \in G$, with inverse $g^{-1}$.
Then:
:$\paren {g^{-1} }^{-1} = g$

items.title: Inverse of Group Isomorphism is Isomorphism
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups.
Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a mapping.
Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism {{iff}} $\phi^{-1}: \struct {H, *} \to \struct {G, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

items.title: Inverse of Group Product
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$.
Let $a, b \in G$, with inverses $a^{-1}, b^{-1}$.
Then:
:$\paren {a \circ b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \circ a^{-1}$

items.title: Inverse of Group Product/General Result
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$.
Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \in G$, with inverses $a_1^{-1}, a_2^{-1}, \ldots, a_n^{-1}$.
Then:
:$\paren {a_1 \circ a_2 \circ \cdots \circ a_n}^{-1} = a_n^{-1} \circ \cdots \circ a_2^{-1} \circ a_1^{-1}$

items.title: Inverse of Injective and Surjective Mapping is Mapping
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that:
:$(1): \quad f$ is an injection
:$(2): \quad f$ is a surjection.
Then the inverse $f^{-1}$ of $f$ is itself a mapping.

items.title: Inverse of Inverse of Bijection
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection.
Then:
:$\paren {f^{-1} }^{-1} = f$
where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse of $f$.

items.title: Inverse of Matrix is Scalar Product of Adjugate by Reciprocal of Determinant
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a nonsingular square matrix of order $n$.
Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$.
Let $\adj {\mathbf A}$ be the adjugate of $\mathbf A$.
Then:
:$\mathbf A^{-1} = \dfrac 1 {\map \det {\mathbf A} } \cdot \adj {\mathbf A}$
where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathbf A$

items.title: Inverse of Product of Subsets of Group
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $X, Y \subseteq G$.
Then:
:$\paren {X \circ Y}^{-1} = Y^{-1} \circ X^{-1}$
where $X^{-1}$ is the inverse of $X$.

items.title: Inverse of Transitive Relation is Transitive
items.statement:
Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$.
Let $\RR$ be transitive.
Then its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is also transitive.

items.title: Inverse of Vandermonde Matrix
items.statement:
Let $V_n$ be the Vandermonde matrix of order $n$ given by:
:<nowiki>$V_n = \begin {bmatrix}
  x_1 & x_2 & \cdots & x_n \\
  x_1^2 & x_2^2 & \cdots & x_n^2 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
  x_1^n & x_2^n & \cdots & x_n^n
\end{bmatrix}$</nowiki>
Then its inverse $V_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as:
:<nowiki>$b_{i j} = \begin {cases}
\paren {-1}^{j - 1} \paren {\dfrac {\ds \sum_{\substack {1 \mathop \le m_1 \mathop < \ldots \mathop < m_{n - j} \mathop \le n \\ m_1, \ldots, m_{n - j} \mathop \ne i} } x_{m_1} \cdots x_{m_{n - j} } } {x_i \ds \prod_{\substack {1 \mathop \le m \mathop \le n \\ m \mathop \ne i} } \paren {x_m - x_i} } } & : 1 \le  j < n \\
\qquad \qquad \qquad \dfrac 1 {x_i \ds \prod_{\substack {1 \mathop \le m \mathop \le n \\ m \mathop \ne i} } \paren {x_i - x_m} } & : j = n
\end{cases}$</nowiki>

items.title: Inverses in Group Direct Product
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of the two groups $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$.
Let $g^{-1}$ be an inverse of $g \in \struct {G, \circ_1}$.
Let $h^{-1}$ be an inverse of $h \in \struct {H, \circ_2}$.
Then $\tuple {g^{-1}, h^{-1} }$ is the inverse of $\tuple {g, h} \in \struct {G \times H, \circ}$.

items.title: Inversion Mapping Reverses Ordering in Ordered Group
Inversion Mapping Reverses Ordering in Ordered Group/Corollary
Inversion Mapping is Permutation
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$.
Then $\iota$ is a permutation on $G$.

items.title: Isolated Point of Closure of Subset is Isolated Point of Subset
items.statement:
Let $\struct {T, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $H \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$.
Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$.
Let $x \in \map \cl H$ be an isolated point of $\map \cl H$.
Then $x$ is also an isolated point of $H$.

items.title: Isometry Preserves Sequence Convergence
items.statement:
Let $M_1 = \struct {S_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {S_2, d_2}$ both be metric spaces or pseudometric spaces.
Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ be an isometry.
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be an infinite sequence in $S_1$.
Suppose that $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to a point $p \in S_1$.
Then $\sequence {\map \phi {x_n}}$ converges to $\map \phi p$.

items.title: Isomorphic Ordinals are Equal
items.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be ordinals that are order isomorphic.
Then $A = B$.

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Associativity
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism.
Then $\circ$ is associative {{iff}} $*$ is associative.

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Commutativity
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism.
Then $\circ$ is commutative {{iff}} $*$ is commutative.

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Groups
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism.
If $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group, then so is $\struct {T, *}$.

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Identity
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism.
Then $\circ$ has an identity $e_S$ {{iff}} $\map \phi {e_S}$ is the identity for $*$.

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Inverses
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism.
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$.
Then $x^{-1}$ is an inverse of $x$ for $\circ$ {{iff}} $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse of $\map \phi x$ for $*$.
That is, {{iff}}:
:$\map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$

items.title: Isomorphism Preserves Semigroups
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures.
Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an isomorphism.
If $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a semigroup, then so is $\struct {T, *}$.

items.title: Isomorphism between Gaussian Integer Units and Integers Modulo 4 under Addition
items.statement:
Let $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ be the group of Gaussian integer units under complex multiplication.
Let $\struct {\Z_n, +_4}$ be the integers modulo $4$ under modulo addition.
Then $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ and $\struct {\Z_4, +_4}$ are isomorphic algebraic structures.

items.title: Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
items.statement:
Isomorphism is an equivalence on a set of magmas.
This result applies to all magmas: rings, groups, R-algebraic structures etc.

items.title: Jensen's Formula
items.statement:
Let $S$ be an open subset of the complex plane containing the closed disk:
:$D_r = \set {z \in \C : \cmod z \le r}$
of radius $r$ about $0$.
Let $f: S \to \C$ be holomorphic on $S$. 
Let $f$ have no zeroes on the circle $\cmod z = r$.
Let $\map f 0 \ne 0$.
Let $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_n$ be the zeroes of $f$ in $D_r$, counted with multiplicity.
Then:
:$(1): \quad \ds \frac 1 {2 \pi} \int_0^{2 \pi} \ln \cmod {\map f {r e^{i \theta} } } \rd \theta = \ln \cmod {\map f 0} + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {\ln r - \ln \size {\rho_k} }$

items.title: Join Semilattice is Ordered Structure
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice.
Then $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ is an ordered structure.
That is, $\preceq$ is compatible with $\vee$.

items.title: Kernel of Character on Unital Commutative Banach Algebra is Maximal Ideal
items.statement:
Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital commutative Banach algebra over $\C$. 
Let $\phi : A \to \C$ be a character on $A$. 
Then $\ker \phi$ is a maximal ideal of $A$.

items.title: Klein Four-Group and Group of Cyclic Group of Order 4 are not Isomorphic
items.statement: The Klein $4$-group $K_4$ and the cyclic group of order $4$ $C_4$ are not isomorphic.

items.title: Klein Four-Group is Normal in A4
items.statement:
Let $A_4$ denote the alternating group on $4$ letters, whose Cayley table is given as:
{{:Alternating Group on 4 Letters/Cayley Table}}
The subsets of $A_4$ which form subgroups of $A_4$ are as follows:
Consider the order $4$ subgroup $V$ of $A_4$, presented by Cayley table:
:<nowiki>$\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\circ & e & t & u & v \\
\hline
e & e & t & u & v \\
t & t & e & v & u \\
u & u & v & e & t \\
v & v & u & t & e \\
\end{array}$</nowiki>
Then $V$ is normal in $A_4$.
Its index is:
:$\index {A_4} V = \dfrac {\order {A_4} } {\order V} = \dfrac {12} 4 = 3$
The (left) cosets of $V$ are:
:$V$
:$A := a V$
:$P := p V$
and the Cayley table of the quotient group $A_4 / V$ is given by:
:<nowiki>$\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\circ & V & A & P \\
\hline
V & V & A & P \\
A & A & P & V \\
P & P & V & A \\
\end{array}$</nowiki>
Note that while $A_4 / V$ is Abelian, $A_4$ is not.

items.title: Knaster-Tarski Lemma
items.statement:
Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice.
Let $f: L \to L$ be an increasing mapping.
Then $f$ has a smallest fixed point and a greatest fixed point.

items.title: Knaster-Tarski Lemma/Corollary
items.statement:
Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice.
Let $f: L \to L$ be an increasing mapping.
Then $f$ has a fixed point

items.title: Knaster-Tarski Lemma/Corollary/Power Set
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$.
Let $f: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ be a $\subseteq$-increasing mapping.
That is, suppose that for all $T, U \in \powerset S$:
:$T \subseteq U \implies \map f T \subseteq \map f U$
Then $f$ has a fixed point.

items.title: Kummer's Hypergeometric Theorem
items.statement: :$\map F {n, -x; x + n + 1; -1} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {x + n + 1} \map \Gamma {\dfrac n 2 + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x + \dfrac n 2 + 1} \map \Gamma {n + 1} }$

items.title: Kuratowski's Closure-Complement Problem
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$.
By successive applications of the operations of complement relative to $S$ and the closure, there can be as many as $14$ distinct subsets of $S$ (including $A$ itself).

items.title: König's Tree Lemma
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a rooted tree with an infinite number of nodes, each with a finite number of children.
Then $T$ has a branch of infinite length.

items.title: L'Hôpital's Rule
items.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$.
Let:
:$\forall x \in \openint a b: \map {g'} x \ne 0$
where $g'$ denotes the derivative of $g$ {{WRT|Differentiation}} $x$.
Let:
:$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map f x = \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map g x = 0$
Then:
:$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \frac {\map f x} {\map g x} = \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \frac {\map {f'} x} {\map {g'} x}$
provided that the second limit exists.

items.title: LCM from Prime Decomposition
Lagrange's Four Square Theorem
items.statement: Every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of four squares.

items.title: Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.
Then:
:$\order H$ divides $\order G$
where $\order G$ and $\order H$ are the order of $G$ and $H$ respectively.
In fact:
:$\index G H = \dfrac {\order G} {\order H}$
where $\index G H$ is the index of $H$ in $G$.
When $G$ is an infinite group, we can still interpret this theorem sensibly:
:A subgroup of finite index in an infinite group is itself an infinite group.
:A finite subgroup of an infinite group has infinite index.

items.title: Lagrange's Trigonometric Identities/Sine/Sine Form
Laplace Transform of Bessel Function of the First Kind
items.statement:
Let $J_n$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$.
Then the Laplace transform of $J_n$ is given as:
:$\laptrans {\map {J_n} {a t} } = \dfrac {\paren {\sqrt {s^2 + a^2} - s}^n} {a^n \sqrt {s^2 + a^2} }$

items.title: Laplace Transform of Bessel Function of the First Kind of Order Zero
items.statement:
Let $J_0$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$.
Then the Laplace transform of $J_0$ is given as:
:$\laptrans {\map {J_0} t} = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {s^2 + 1} }$

items.title: Laplace Transform of Constant Mapping
items.statement:
Let $a \in \R$ be a real constant.
Let $f_a: \R \to \R$ or $\C$ be the constant mapping, defined as:
:$\forall t \in \R: \map {f_a} t = a$
Let $\laptrans {f_a}$ be the Laplace transform of $f_a$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {\map {f_a} t} = \dfrac a s$
for $\map \Re s > a$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Cosine
items.statement:
Let $\cos$ be the real cosine function.
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {\cos a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 + a^2}$
where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Dirac Delta Function
items.statement:
Let $\map \delta t$ denote the Dirac delta function.
The Laplace transform of $\map \delta t$ is given by:
:$\laptrans {\map \delta t} = 1$

items.title: Laplace Transform of Exponential/Real Argument
items.statement:
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$.
Let $e^x$ be the real exponential.
Then:
:$\map {\laptrans {e^{a t} } } s = \dfrac 1 {s - a}$
where $a \in \R$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > \map \Re a$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Gauss Error Function
items.statement:
:$\laptrans {\map \erf t} = \dfrac 1 s \map \exp {\dfrac {s^2} 4} \map \erfc {\dfrac s 2}$
where:
:$\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$
:$\erf$ denotes the Gauss error function
:$\erfc$ denotes the complementary error function
:$\exp$ denotes the exponential function.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Heaviside Step Function
items.statement:
Let $\map {u_c} t$ denote the Heaviside step function:
:<nowiki>$\map {u_c} t = \begin {cases}
1 & : t > c \\
0 & : t < c
\end {cases}$</nowiki>
The Laplace transform of $\map {u_c} t$ is given by:
:$\laptrans {\map {u_c} t} = \dfrac {e^{-s c} } s$
for $\map \Re s > c$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Cosine
items.statement:
Let $\cosh t$ be the hyperbolic cosine, where $t$ is real.
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {\cosh a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 - a^2}$
where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Sine
items.statement:
Let $\sinh t$ be the hyperbolic sine, where $t$ is real.
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {\sinh a t} = \dfrac a {s^2 - a^2}$
where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Periodic Function
items.statement:
Let $f$ be periodic, that is:
:$\exists T \in \R_{\ne 0}: \forall x \in \R: \map f x = \map f {x + T}$
Then:
:$\laptrans {\map f t} = \dfrac 1 {1 - e^{-s T} } \ds \int_0^T e^{-s t} \map f t \rd t$
where $\laptrans {\map f t}$ denotes the Laplace transform.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Positive Integer Power
items.statement:
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$.
Let $t^n: \R \to \R$ be $t$ to the $n$th power for some $n \in \N_{\ge 0}$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {t^n} = \dfrac {n!} {s^{n + 1} }$
for $\map \Re s > 0$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Sine
items.statement:
Let $\sin$ denote the real sine function.
Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a real function $f$.
Then:
:$\laptrans {\sin at} = \dfrac a {s^2 + a^2}$
where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > 0$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of Sine Integral Function
items.statement:
:$\laptrans {\map \Si t} = \dfrac 1 s \arctan \dfrac 1 s$
where:
:$\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$
:$\Si$ denotes the sine integral function

items.title: Laplace Transform of Sine of Root
items.statement:
:$\laptrans {\sin \sqrt t} = \dfrac {\sqrt \pi} {2 s^{3/2} } \map \exp {-\dfrac 1 {4 s} }$
where $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$.

items.title: Laplace Transform of t sine a t
items.statement: :$\map {\laptrans {t \sin a t} } s = \dfrac {2 a s} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$

items.title: Law of Cosines
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$.
Then:
:$c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 a b \cos C$

items.title: Law of Excluded Middle/Sequent Form
items.statement:
The '''Law of Excluded Middle''' can be symbolised by the sequent:
:$\vdash p \lor \neg p$

items.title: Law of Identity
Law of Identity/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \vdash p$

items.title: Law of Identity/Formulation 2
items.statement:
Every proposition entails itself:
:$\vdash p \implies p$

items.title: Law of Sines
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$.
Then:
:$\dfrac a {\sin A} = \dfrac b {\sin B} = \dfrac c {\sin C} = 2 R$
where $R$ is the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$.

items.title: Law of Tangents
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$.
Then:
:$\dfrac {a + b} {a - b} = \dfrac {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A + B} } {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A - B} }$

items.title: Least Upper Bound Property
items.statement:
Let $S \subset \R$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers such that $S$ is bounded above.
Then $S$ admits a supremum in $\R$.
This is known as the '''least upper bound property''' of the real numbers.

items.title: Left and Right Coset Spaces are Equivalent
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.
Let:
:$x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$
:$H y$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $y$.
Then:
:$\order {\set {x H: x \in G} } = \order {\set {H y: y \in G} }$

items.title: Left and Right Inverse Mappings Implies Bijection
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $f$ be such that:
: $\exists g_1: T \to S: g_1 \circ f = I_S$
: $\exists g_2: T \to S: f \circ g_2 = I_T$
where both $g_1$ and $g_2$ are mappings.
Then $f$ is a bijection.

items.title: Left and Right Inverses of Mapping are Inverse Mapping
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that:
:$(1): \quad \exists g_1: T \to S: g_1 \circ f = I_S$
:$(2): \quad \exists g_2: T \to S: f \circ g_2 = I_T$
Then:
: $g_1 = g_2 = f^{-1}$
where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse of $f$.

items.title: Legendre's Duplication Formula
items.statement:
:$\forall z \notin \set {-\dfrac n 2: n \in \N}: \map \Gamma z \map \Gamma {z + \dfrac 1 2} = 2^{1 - 2 z} \sqrt \pi \, \map \Gamma {2 z}$
where $\N$ denotes the natural numbers.

items.title: Leibniz's Formula for Pi
items.statement: :$\dfrac \pi 4 = 1 - \dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 1 5 - \dfrac 1 7 + \dfrac 1 9 - \cdots \approx 0 \cdotp 78539 \, 81633 \, 9744 \ldots$

items.title: Lemniscate of Bernoulli is Special Case of Ovals of Cassini
items.statement: The lemniscate of Bernoulli is a special case of the ovals of Cassini.

items.title: Length of Angle Bisector
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle.
Let $AD$ be the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$ in $\triangle ABC$.
:300px
Let $d$ be the length of $AD$.
Then $d$ is given by:
:$d^2 = \dfrac {b c} {\paren {b + c}^2} \paren {\paren {b + c}^2 - a^2}$
where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are the sides opposite $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively.

items.title: Length of Arc of Cycloid
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations:
:$x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$
:$y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$
Then the length of one arc of the cycloid is $8 a$.

items.title: Length of Chord of Circle
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a circle of radius $r$.
Let $AB$ be a chord which joins the endpoints of the arc $ADB$.
Then:
:$AB = 2 r \sin \dfrac \theta 2$
where $\theta$ is the angle subtended by $AB$ at the center of $C$.

items.title: Length of Perimeter of Cardioid
items.statement:
Consider the cardioid $C$ embedded in a polar plane given by its polar equation:
:$r = 2 a \paren {1 + \cos \theta}$
where $a > 0$.
The length of the perimeter of $C$ is $16 a$.

items.title: Limit Points of Open Set of Particular Point Space
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space.
Let $U \subseteq S$ such that $p \in U$.
Let $x \in S$ such that $x \ne p$.
Then $x$ is a limit point of $U$.

items.title: Limit of (Cosine (X) - 1) over X at Zero
items.statement: :$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0} \frac {\cos x - 1} x = 0$

items.title: Limit of Integer to Reciprocal Power
items.statement:
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the real sequence defined as $x_n = n^{1/n}$, using exponentiation.
Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges with a limit of $1$.

items.title: Limit of Root of Positive Real Number
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R: x > 0$ be a real number.
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as:
:$x_n = x^{1 / n}$
Then $x_n \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$.

items.title: Limit of Sinc Function at Zero
items.statement: :$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0} \frac {\sin x} x = 1$

items.title: Limit of Tan X over X at Zero
items.statement: :$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0} \frac {\tan x} x = 1$

items.title: Limit of x to the x
items.statement:
Let $f: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be defined as:
:$\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \map f x = x^x$
Then:
:$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0^+} x^x = 1$

items.title: Linear Combination of Integrals
items.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be real numbers.
Then the following results hold:

items.title: Linear Combination of Integrals/Definite
items.statement: :$\ds \int_a^b \paren {\lambda \map f t + \mu \map g t} \rd t = \lambda \int_a^b \map f t \rd t + \mu \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$

items.title: Linear First Order ODE/x dy + y dx = x cosine x dx
items.statement:
The linear first order ODE:
:$x \rd y + y \rd x = x \cos x \rd x$
has the general solution:
:$x y = x \sin x + \cos x + C$

items.title: Linear First Order ODE/x y' + y = x^2 cosine x
items.statement:
The linear first order ODE:
:$x \, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + y = x^2 \cos x$
has the general solution:
:$y = 2 \cos x + x \sin x - \dfrac 2 x \sin x + \dfrac C x$

items.title: Linear Function is Continuous
items.statement:
Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be real numbers.
Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a linear real function:
:$\map f x = \alpha x + \beta$
for all $x \in \R$.
Then $f$ is continuous at every real number $c \in \R$.

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/(x^2 + x) y'' + (2 - x^2) y' - (2 + x) y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad \paren {x^2 + x} y' ' + \paren {2 - x^2} y' - \paren {2 + x} y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^x + \dfrac {C_2} x$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + 2 x y' - 2 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x^2 y'' + 2 x y' - 2 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 x + \dfrac {C_2} {x^2}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + x y' - 4 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x^2 y'' + x y' - 4 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 x^2 + \dfrac {C_2} {x^2}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + x y' - y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x^2 y'' + x y' - y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 x + \dfrac {C_2} x$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad x^2 y' ' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 x + C_2 x^2$
on any closed real interval which does not contain $0$.

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 8 x^2 - 4 x
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y'' + 4 y = 8 x^2 - 4 x$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 \sin 2 x + C_2 \cos 2 x - 1 - x + 2 x^2$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + k^2 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' + k^2 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = A \, \map \sin {k x + B}$
or can be expressed as:
:$y = C_1 \sin k x + C_2 \cos k x$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' + y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + y = 2 x
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' + y = 2 x$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^x + C_2 x e^x + 2 x + 4$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 3 y' + 2 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - 3 y' + 2 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{2 x}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y' + 4 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - 4 y' + 4 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 x e^{2 x}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - 4 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - k^2 y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - k^2 y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^{k x} + C_2 e^{-k x}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y' - 6 y = exp -x
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y'' - y' - 6 y = e^{-x}$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x} - \dfrac {e^{-x} } 4$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y = 0
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' - y = 0$
has the general solution:
:$y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{-x}$

items.title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' = y'
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y'' = y'$
has the general solution:
:$y = A_1 e^x + A_2$

items.title: Linear Span is Linear Subspace
items.statement:
Let $V$ be a vector space over a division ring $K$.
Let $S \subseteq V$ be a subset of $V$.
Then the linear span $\map \span S$ is a subspace of $V$.

items.title: Linear Transformation Maps Zero Vector to Zero Vector
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0$.
Likewise let $\mathbf V\,'$ be another vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0'$.
Let $T: \mathbf V \to \mathbf V\,'$ be a linear transformation.
Then:
:$T: \mathbf 0 \mapsto \mathbf 0'$

items.title: Linear Transformation of Arithmetic Mean
items.statement:
Let $D = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ be a set of real data describing a quantitative variable.
Let $\overline x$ be the arithmetic mean of the data in $D$.
Let $T: \R \to \R$ be a linear transformation such that:
:$\forall i \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, n}: \map T {x_i} = \lambda x_i + \gamma$
Let $T \sqbrk D$ be the image of $D$ under $T$.
Then the arithmetic mean of the data in $T \sqbrk D$ is given by:
:$\map T {\overline x} = \lambda \overline x + \gamma$

items.title: Linearly Independent Set is Contained in some Basis/Finite Dimensional Case
items.statement:
Let $E$ be a vector space of $n$ dimensions.
Let $H$ be a linearly independent subset of $E$.
There exists a basis $B$ for $E$ such that $H \subseteq B$.

items.title: Liouville's Theorem (Complex Analysis)
items.statement:
Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a bounded entire function.
Then $f$ is constant.

items.title: Lipschitz Equivalent Metrics are Topologically Equivalent
items.statement:
Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$.
Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be Lipschitz equivalent.
Then $d_1$ and $d_2$ are topologically equivalent.

items.title: Locally Euclidean Space is Locally Compact
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$.
Then $M$ is locally compact.

items.title: Log of Gamma Function is Convex on Positive Reals
items.statement:
Let $\Gamma: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be the Gamma function, restricted to the strictly positive real numbers.
Let $\ln$ denote the natural logarithm function.
Then the composite mapping $\ln \circ \operatorname \Gamma$ is a convex function.

items.title: Logarithm Base 10 of 2 is Irrational
items.statement:
The common logarithm of $2$:
:$\log_{10} 2 \approx 0.30102 \, 99956 \, 63981 \, 19521 \, 37389 \ldots$
is irrational.

items.title: Logarithm Tends to Infinity
items.statement: :$\ln x \to +\infty$ as $x \to +\infty$

items.title: Logarithm of Power/Natural Logarithm
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R$ be a strictly positive real number.
Let $a \in \R$ be a real number such that $a > 1$.
Let $r \in \R$ be any real number.
Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$.
Then:
:$\map \ln {x^r} = r \ln x$

items.title: Lower Bound of Natural Logarithm
items.statement:
:$\forall x \in \R_{>0}: 1 - \dfrac 1 x \le \ln x$
where $\ln x$ denotes the natural logarithm of $x$.

items.title: Lower Closure is Lower Section
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set.
Let $T$ be a subset of $S$.
Let $L$ be the lower closure of $T$.
Then $L$ is a lower section.

items.title: Machin's Formula for Pi
items.statement: :$\dfrac \pi 4 = 4 \arctan \dfrac 1 5 - \arctan \dfrac 1 {239} \approx 0 \cdotp 78539 \, 81633 \, 9744 \ldots$

items.title: Magic Constant of Order 3 Magic Square
items.statement: The magic constant of the order $3$ magic square is $15$.

items.title: Magic Constant of Order 4 Magic Square
items.statement: The magic constant of the order $4$ magic square is $34$.

items.title: Mapping from Totally Ordered Set is Order Embedding iff Strictly Increasing
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be a totally ordered set.
Let $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be an ordered set.
Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then $\phi$ is an order embedding {{iff}} $\phi$ is strictly increasing.
That is:
:$\forall x, y \in S: x \preceq_1 y \iff \map \phi x \preceq_2 \map \phi y$
{{iff}}:
:$\forall x, y \in S: x \prec_1 y \implies \map \phi x \prec_2 \map \phi y$

items.title: Mapping from Totally Ordered Set is Order Embedding iff Strictly Increasing/Reverse Implication
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be a totally ordered set.
Let $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be an ordered set.
Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a strictly increasing mapping.
Then $\phi$ is an order embedding.

items.title: Mapping is Injection and Surjection iff Inverse is Mapping
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then:
: $f: S \to T$ can be defined as a bijection in the sense that:
::$(1): \quad f$ is an injection
::$(2): \quad f$ is a surjection
{{iff}}:
:the inverse $f^{-1}$ of $f$ is itself a mapping.

items.title: Matrix Entrywise Addition is Associative
items.statement:
Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over one of the standard number systems.
For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A + \mathbf B$ be defined as the matrix entrywise sum of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
The operation $+$ is associative on $\map \MM {m, n}$.
That is:
:$\paren {\mathbf A + \mathbf B} + \mathbf C = \mathbf A + \paren {\mathbf B + \mathbf C}$
for all $\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B$ and $\mathbf C$ in $\map \MM {m, n}$.

items.title: Matrix Entrywise Addition is Commutative
items.statement:
Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over one of the standard number systems.
For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A + \mathbf B$ be defined as the matrix entrywise sum of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
The operation $+$ is commutative on $\map \MM {m, n}$.
That is:
:$\mathbf A + \mathbf B = \mathbf B + \mathbf A$
for all $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ in $\map \MM {m, n}$.

items.title: Matrix Entrywise Addition over Ring is Associative
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring.
Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$.
For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_R} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A + \mathbf B$ be defined as the matrix entrywise sum of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
The operation $+$ is associative on $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$.
That is:
:$\paren {\mathbf A + \mathbf B} + \mathbf C = \mathbf A + \paren {\mathbf B + \mathbf C}$
for all $\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B$ and $\mathbf C$ in $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$.

items.title: Matrix Entrywise Addition over Ring is Closed
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring.
Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$.
For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_R} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A + \mathbf B$ be defined as the matrix entrywise sum of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
The operation $+$ is closed on $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$.

items.title: Matrix Entrywise Addition over Ring is Commutative
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring.
Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$.
For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_R} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A + \mathbf B$ be defined as the matrix entrywise sum of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$.
The operation $+$ is commutative on $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$.
That is:
:$\mathbf A + \mathbf B = \mathbf B + \mathbf A$
for all $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ in $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$.

items.title: Matrix Similarity is Equivalence Relation
items.statement: Matrix similarity is an equivalence relation.

items.title: Matroid Unique Circuit Property
items.statement:
Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid.
Let $X \subseteq S$ be an independent subset of $M$.
Let $x \in S$ such that:
:$X \cup \set x$ is a dependent subset of $M$.
Then there exists a unique circuit $C$ such that:
:$x \in C \subseteq X \cup \set x$

items.title: Max and Min of Function on Closed Real Interval
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Then $f$ reaches a maximum and a minimum on $\closedint a b$.

items.title: Maximal Ideal iff Quotient Ring is Field
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$.
Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$.
The following are equivalent:
:$(1): \quad$ $J$ is a maximal ideal.
:$(2): \quad$ The quotient ring $R / J$ is a field.

items.title: Mean Value Theorem
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$.
Then:
:$\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map {f'} \xi = \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {b - a}$

items.title: Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a continuous real function on the closed interval $\closedint a b$.
Then there exists a real number $k \in \closedint a b$ such that:
:$\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \map f k \paren {b - a}$

items.title: Measure is Monotone
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space.
Then $\mu$ is monotone, that is:
:$\forall E, F \in \Sigma: E \subseteq F \implies \map \mu E \le \map \mu F$

items.title: Median Formula
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle.
Let $CD$ be the median of $\triangle ABC$ which bisects $AB$.
:400px
The length $m_c$ of $CD$ is given by:
:${m_c}^2 = \dfrac {a^2 + b^2} 2 - \dfrac {c^2} 4$

items.title: Mediant is Between
items.statement:
Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers such that $b > 0, d > 0$.
Let $r = \dfrac a b < \dfrac c d = s$.
Then:
:$r < \dfrac {a + c} {b + d} < s$

items.title: Metric Space Completeness is Preserved by Isometry
items.statement:
Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces.
Let $\phi: M_1 \to M_2$ be an isometry.
If $M_1$ is complete then so is $M_2$.

items.title: Metric Space is Paracompact
items.statement:
Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space.
Then $M$ is a paracompact space.

items.title: Metric Space is Regular
items.statement: A metric space $M = \struct {A, d}$ is a regular space.

items.title: Metric Space is T2
items.statement: A metric space $M = \struct {A, d}$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

items.title: Metric Space is T4
items.statement: A metric space $M = \struct {A, d}$ is a $T_4$ space.

items.title: Minimal Polynomial Exists
items.statement:
Let $L / K$ be a field extension.
Let $\alpha \in L$ be algebraic over $K$.
Then there exists a minimal polynomial $f \in K \sqbrk x$ for $\alpha$ over $K$.

items.title: Minimal Polynomial is Unique
items.statement:
Let $L / K$ be a field extension.
Let $\alpha \in L$ be algebraic over $K$.
Then the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$ is unique.

items.title: Minimally Closed Class under Progressing Mapping
Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping induces Nest
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$.
Then $M$ is a nest in which:
:$\forall x, y \in M: \map g x \subseteq y \lor y \subseteq x$

items.title: Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping is Well-Ordered under Subset Relation
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$.
Let $x$ be a fixed point of $g$.
Then $M$ is well-ordered under the subset relation.

items.title: Minimally Inductive Set is Ordinal
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ denote the minimally inductive set.
Then $\omega$ is an ordinal.

items.title: Minkowski's Inequality for Sums
items.statement:
Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n, b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be non-negative real numbers.
Let $p \in \R$, $p \ne 0$ be a real number.
If $p < 0$, then we require that $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n, b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$ be strictly positive.
If $p > 1$, then:
:$\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {a_k + b_k}^p}^{1/p} \le \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^p}^{1/p} + \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n b_k^p}^{1/p}$
If $p < 1$, $p \ne 0$, then:
:$\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {a_k + b_k}^p}^{1/p} \ge \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^p}^{1/p} + \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n b_k^p}^{1/p}$

items.title: Minkowski's Inequality for Sums/Index Greater than 1
items.statement:
Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n, b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be non-negative real numbers.
Let $p \in \R$ be a real number such that $p > 1$.
Then:
:$\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {a_k + b_k}^p}^{1 / p} \le \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n {a_k}^p}^{1 / p} + \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n {b_k}^p}^{1 / p}$

items.title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Cotangent Function
items.statement:
:$\ds \pi \cot \pi z = \frac 1 z + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac z {z^2 - n^2}$
where:
:$z \in \C$ is not an integer
:$\cot$ is the cotangent function.

items.title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Tangent Function
items.statement:
:$\ds \pi \map \tan {\pi z} = 8 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac z {\paren {2 n + 1}^2 - 4 z^2}$
where: 
:$z \in \C$ is not a half-integer
:$\tan$ is the tangent function.

items.title: Module on Cartesian Product is Module
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring.
Let $n \in \N_{>0}$.
Let $\struct {R^n, +, \times}_R$ be the '''$R$-module $R^n$'''.
Then $\struct {R^n, +, \times}_R$ is an $R$-module.

items.title: Module on Cartesian Product of Ring with Unity is Unitary Module
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity.
Let $n \in \N_{>0}$.
Let $\struct {R^n, +, \times}_R$ be the '''$R$-module $R^n$'''.
Then $\struct {R^n, +, \times}_R$ is a unitary $R$-module.

items.title: Modulo Addition is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer.
Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$.
Let $\eqclass a m$ denote the equivalence class on $\Z_m$, for some $a \in \Z$.
The modulo addition operation on $\Z_m$, defined by the rule:
:$\eqclass a m +_m \eqclass b m = \eqclass {a + b} m$
is a well-defined operation.
That is:
:If $a \equiv b \pmod m$ and $x \equiv y \pmod m$, then $a + x \equiv b + y \pmod m$.

items.title: Modulo Multiplication is Associative
items.statement:
Multiplication modulo $m$ is associative:
:$\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m, \eqclass z m \in \Z_m: \paren {\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m} \times_m \eqclass z m = \eqclass x m \times_m \paren {\eqclass y m \times_m \eqclass z m}$
That is:
:$\forall x, y, z \in \Z_m: \paren {x \cdot_m y} \cdot_m z = x \cdot_m \paren {y \cdot_m z}$

items.title: Modulo Multiplication is Well-Defined
items.statement:
The multiplication modulo $m$ operation on $\Z_m$, the set of integers modulo $m$, defined by the rule:
:$\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m = \eqclass {x y} m$
is a well-defined operation.
That is:
:If $a \equiv b \pmod m$ and $x \equiv y \pmod m$, then $a x \equiv b y \pmod m$.

items.title: Modus Ponendo Ponens/Sequent Form
Modus Ponendo Ponens/Variant 2
items.statement: :$\vdash p \implies \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies q}$

items.title: Modus Ponendo Ponens/Variant 3
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \land p} \implies q$

items.title: Modus Tollendo Ponens/Variant/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \lor q} \iff \paren {\neg p \implies q}$

items.title: Motion of Rocket in Outer Space
items.statement:
