items.title: Real Numbers are Uncountably Infinite
items.statement: The set of real numbers $\R$ is uncountably infinite.

items.title: Real Numbers form Ordered Integral Domain
items.statement: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms an ordered integral domain under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times, \le}$.

items.title: Reciprocal Function is Strictly Decreasing
items.statement:
The reciprocal function:
:$\operatorname{recip}: \R \setminus \set 0 \to \R$, $x \mapsto \dfrac 1 x$
is strictly decreasing:
:on the open interval $\openint 0 \to$
:on the open interval $\openint \gets 0$

items.title: Reciprocal Sequence is Strictly Decreasing
items.statement:
The reciprocal sequence:
:$\sequence {\operatorname {recip} }: \N_{>0} \to \R$: $n \mapsto \dfrac 1 n$
is strictly decreasing.

items.title: Reciprocal of Logarithm
items.statement:
Let $x, y \in \R_{> 0}$ be (strictly) positive real numbers.
Then:
:$\dfrac 1 {\log_x y} = \log_y x$

items.title: Reciprocal of One Minus Cosine
items.statement: :$\dfrac 1 {1 - \cos x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\csc^2} {\dfrac x 2}$

items.title: Reciprocal of One Plus Cosine
items.statement: :$\dfrac 1 {1 + \cos x} = \dfrac 1 2 \sec^2 \dfrac x 2$

items.title: Reciprocal times Derivative of Gamma Function
items.statement:
Let $z \in \C \setminus \Z_{\le 0}$.
Then:
:$\ds \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} z} {\map \Gamma z} = -\gamma + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\frac 1 n - \frac 1 {z + n - 1} }$
where:
:$\map \Gamma z$ denotes the Gamma function
:$\map {\Gamma'} z$ denotes the derivative of the Gamma function
:$\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

items.title: Reduced Residue System under Multiplication forms Abelian Group
items.statement:
Let $\Z_m$ be the set of set of residue classes modulo $m$.
Let $\struct {\Z'_m, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $m$.
Then $\struct {\Z'_m, \times}$ is an abelian group, precisely equal to the group of units of $\Z_m$.

items.title: Reductio ad Absurdum/Variant 1
items.statement: :$\neg p \implies \bot \vdash p$

items.title: Reductio ad Absurdum/Variant 2
items.statement: :$\neg p \implies \paren {q \land \neg q} \vdash p$

items.title: Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Sine
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer.
Let:
:$I_n := \ds \int \sin^n x \rd x$
Then:
:$I_n = \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2} - \dfrac {\sin^{n - 1} x \cos x} n$
is a reduction formula for $\ds \int \sin^n x \rd x$.

items.title: Reflexive Closure is Closure Operator
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $R$ be the set of all endorelations on $S$.
Then the reflexive closure operator on $R$ is a closure operator.

items.title: Reflexive Reduction of Ordering is Strict Ordering
items.statement:
Let $\RR$ be an ordering on a set $S$.
Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$.
Then $\RR^\ne$ is a strict ordering on $S$.

items.title: Reflexive and Symmetric Relation is not necessarily Transitive
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\alpha \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$.
Let $\alpha$ be both reflexive and symmetric.
Then it is not necessarily the case that $\alpha$ is also transitive.

items.title: Regular Paracompact Space is not necessarily Metrizable
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is regular and paracompact.
Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is metrizable.

items.title: Relation between Two Ordinals
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be ordinals.
Then either $S \subseteq T$ or $T \subseteq S$.

items.title: Relative Complement of Cartesian Product
items.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be sets.
Let $X \subseteq A$ and $Y \subseteq B$.
Then:
:$\relcomp {A \mathop \times B} {X \times Y} = \paren {A \times \relcomp B Y} \cup \paren {\relcomp A X \times B}$

items.title: Relative Complement of Relative Complement
items.statement: :$\relcomp S {\relcomp S T} = T$

items.title: Relative Matrix of Composition of Linear Transformations
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring with unity.
Let $M, N, P$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $m, n, p > 0$ respectively.
Let $\AA, \BB, \CC$ be ordered bases of $M, N, P$.
Let $f: M \to N$ and $g : N \to P$ be linear transformations, and $g \circ f$ be their composition.
Let $\mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$ and $\mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB}$ be their matrices relative to $\AA, \BB$ and $\BB, \CC$ respectively.
Then the matrix of $g \circ f$ relative to $\AA$ and $\CC$ is:
:$\mathbf M_{g \mathop \circ f, \CC, \AA} = \mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB} \cdot \mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$

items.title: Renaming Mapping is Bijection
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f$ be the renaming mapping, defined as:
:$r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f: \map r {\eqclass x {\RR_f} } = \map f x$
where:
:$\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by the mapping $f$
:$S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR_f$
:$\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR_f$.
The renaming mapping is a bijection.

items.title: Renaming Mapping is Well-Defined
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f$ be the renaming mapping,  defined as:
:$r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f: \map r {\eqclass x {\RR_f} } = \map f x$
where:
:$\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by the mapping $f$
:$S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR_f$
:$\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR_f$.
The renaming mapping is always well-defined.

items.title: Resolvent Mapping is Analytic/Bounded Linear Operator
items.statement:
Let $B$ be a Banach space.
Let $\map \LL {B, B}$ be the set of bounded linear operators from $B$ to itself.
Let $T \in \map \LL {B, B}$.
Let $\map \rho T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ in the complex plane.
Then the resolvent mapping $f : \map \rho T \to \map \LL {B, B}$ given by $\map f z = \paren {T - z I}^{-1}$ is analytic, and:
:$\map {f'} z = \paren {T - z I}^{-2}$
where $f'$ denotes the derivative of $f$ {{WRT|Differentiation}} $z$.

items.title: Reverse Triangle Inequality
Reverse Triangle Inequality/Real and Complex Fields
items.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be elements of either the real numbers $\R$ or the complex numbers $\C$.
Then:
:$\cmod {x - y} \ge \size {\cmod x - \cmod y}$

items.title: Reverse Triangle Inequality/Real and Complex Fields/Corollary 1
items.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be elements of either the real numbers $\R$ or the complex numbers $\C$.
Then:
:$\size {x - y} \ge \size x - \size y$
where $\size x$ denotes either the absolute value of a real number or the complex modulus of a complex number.

items.title: Riemann Zeta Function at Even Integers
Riemann Zeta Function of 4
Riemann Zeta Function of 6
Riesz's Lemma
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a normed vector space.
Let $Y$ be a proper closed linear subspace of $X$. 
Let $\alpha \in \openint 0 1$.
Then there exists $x_\alpha \in X$ such that: 
:$\norm {x_\alpha} = 1$
with:
:$\norm {x_\alpha - y} > \alpha$
for all $y \in Y$.

items.title: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Subrings
items.statement:
Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism.
Let $S$ be a subring of $R_1$.
Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is a subring of $R_2$.

items.title: Ring Homomorphism from Division Ring is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be rings whose zeros are $0_R$ and $0_S$ respectively.
Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism.
If $R$ is a division ring, then either:
:$(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective)
:$(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in R: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

items.title: Ring Homomorphism from Field is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
items.statement:
Let $\struct {F, +_F, \circ}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$.
Let $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_S$.
Let $\phi: F \to S$ be a ring homomorphism.
Then either:
:$(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective)
or
:$(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in F: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

items.title: Ring Zero is Unique
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring.
Then the ring zero of $R$ is unique.

items.title: Ring is Module over Itself
items.statement:
Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring.
Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}_R$ is an $R$-module.

items.title: Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Field
items.statement:
Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$.
Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $m$.
Then:
:$m$ is prime
{{iff}}:
:$\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ is a field.

items.title: Ring of Integers is Principal Ideal Domain
items.statement: The integers $\Z$ form a principal ideal domain.

items.title: Rolle's Theorem
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is:
:continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$
and:
:differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$.
Let $\map f a = \map f b$.
Then:
:$\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map {f'} \xi = 0$

items.title: Rule of Addition/Sequent Form
Rule of Addition/Sequent Form/Formulation 2
Rule of Addition/Sequent Form/Formulation 2/Form 1
items.statement: :$\vdash p \implies \paren {p \lor q}$

items.title: Rule of Association/Conjunction
Rule of Association/Conjunction/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \land \paren {q \land r} \dashv \vdash \paren {p \land q} \land r$

items.title: Rule of Association/Conjunction/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \land \paren {q \land r} } \iff \paren {\paren {p \land q} \land r}$

items.title: Rule of Association/Disjunction
Rule of Association/Disjunction/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \lor \paren {q \lor r} \dashv \vdash \paren {p \lor q} \lor r$

items.title: Rule of Association/Disjunction/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \lor \paren {q \lor r} } \iff \paren {\paren {p \lor q} \lor r}$

items.title: Rule of Commutation/Conjunction
Rule of Commutation/Conjunction/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \land q \dashv \vdash q \land p$

items.title: Rule of Commutation/Disjunction
Rule of Commutation/Disjunction/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \lor q \dashv \vdash q \lor p$

items.title: Rule of Commutation/Disjunction/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \lor q} \iff \paren {q \lor p}$

items.title: Rule of Conjunction/Sequent Form
items.statement: The Rule of Conjunction can be symbolised in sequent form as follows:

items.title: Rule of Conjunction/Sequent Form/Formulation 1
Rule of Distribution/Conjunction Distributes over Disjunction
Rule of Distribution/Conjunction Distributes over Disjunction/Left Distributive
Rule of Distribution/Conjunction Distributes over Disjunction/Left Distributive/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \land \paren {q \lor r} } \iff \paren {\paren {p \land q} \lor \paren {p \land r} }$

items.title: Rule of Distribution/Disjunction Distributes over Conjunction
Rule of Distribution/Disjunction Distributes over Conjunction/Left Distributive
Rule of Distribution/Disjunction Distributes over Conjunction/Left Distributive/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \lor \paren {q \land r} } \iff \paren {\paren {p \lor q} \land \paren {p \lor r} }$

items.title: Rule of Distribution/Disjunction Distributes over Conjunction/Left Distributive/Formulation 2/Forward Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \lor \paren {q \land r} } \implies \paren {\paren {p \lor q} \land \paren {p \lor r} }$

items.title: Rule of Exportation/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$\paren {p \land q} \implies r \dashv \vdash p \implies \paren {q \implies r}$

items.title: Rule of Exportation/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\paren {p \land q} \implies r} \iff \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} }$

items.title: Rule of Exportation/Formulation 2/Forward Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\paren {p \land q} \implies r} \implies \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} }$

items.title: Rule of Exportation/Formulation 2/Reverse Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} } \implies \paren {\paren {p \land q} \implies r}$

items.title: Rule of Idempotence
Rule of Implication/Sequent Form
Rule of Material Equivalence
Rule of Material Equivalence/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \iff q \dashv \vdash \paren {p \implies q} \land \paren {q \implies p}$

items.title: Rule of Material Equivalence/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \iff q} \iff \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \land \paren {q \implies p} }$

items.title: Rule of Material Implication
Rule of Material Implication/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \implies q \dashv \vdash \neg p \lor q$

items.title: Rule of Material Implication/Formulation 1/Reverse Implication
items.statement: :$\neg p \lor q \vdash p \implies q$

items.title: Rule of Material Implication/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies q} \iff \paren {\neg p \lor q}$

items.title: Rule of Simplification/Sequent Form
items.statement: The '''rule of simplification''' can be symbolised by the sequents:

items.title: Rule of Simplification/Sequent Form/Formulation 2
Rule of Transposition/Formulation 1
items.statement:
A statement and its contrapositive have the same truth value:
:$p \implies q \dashv \vdash \neg q \implies \neg p$
Its abbreviation in a tableau proof is $\textrm {TP}$.

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies q} \iff \paren {\neg q \implies \neg p}$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Formulation 2/Forward Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {\neg q \implies \neg p}$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Formulation 2/Reverse Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\neg q \implies \neg p} \implies \paren {p \implies q}$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Variant 1/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \implies \neg q \dashv \vdash q \implies \neg p$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Variant 1/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies \neg q} \iff \paren {q \implies \neg p}$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Variant 2/Formulation 1
items.statement: : $\neg p \implies q \dashv \vdash \neg q \implies p$

items.title: Rule of Transposition/Variant 2/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\neg p \implies q}\ \iff \paren {\neg q \implies p}$

items.title: Russell's Paradox
items.statement: The {{axiom-link|Abstraction}} leads to a contradiction.

items.title: Sandwich Principle
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a class.
Let $g: A \to A$ be a mapping on $A$ such that:
:for all $x, y \in A$, either $\map g x \subseteq y$ or $y \subseteq x$.
Then:
:$\forall x, y \in A: x \subseteq y \subseteq \map g x \implies x = y \lor y = \map g x$
That is, there is no element $y$ of $A$ such that:
:$x \subset y \subset \map g x$
where $\subset$ denotes a proper subset.

items.title: Schröder Rule
items.statement:
Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be relations on a set $S$.
{{TFAE}}
:$(1): \quad A \circ B \subseteq C$
:$(2): \quad A^{-1} \circ \overline C \subseteq \overline B$
:$(3): \quad \overline C \circ B^{-1} \subseteq \overline A$
where:
:$\circ$ denotes relation composition
:$A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $A$
:$\overline A$ denotes the complement of $A$.

items.title: Secant Function is Even
items.statement:
:$\map \sec {-x} = \sec x$
That is, the secant function is even.

items.title: Secant of i
items.statement: :$\sec i = \dfrac {2 e} {e^2 + 1}$

items.title: Second Order ODE/y'' = 1 + (y')^2
items.statement:
The second order ODE:
:$(1): \quad y' ' = 1 + \paren {y'}^2$
has the general solution:
:$y = \map {\ln \sec} {x + C_1} + C_2$

items.title: Second Principle of Mathematical Induction
items.statement:
Let $\map P n$ be a propositional function depending on $n \in \Z$.
Let $n_0 \in \Z$ be given.
Suppose that:
:$(1): \quad \map P {n_0}$ is true
:$(2): \quad \forall k \in \Z: k \ge n_0: \map P {n_0} \land \map P {n_0 + 1} \land \ldots \land \map P {k - 1} \land \map P k \implies \map P {k + 1}$
Then:
:$\map P n$ is true for all $n \ge n_0$.
This process is called '''proof by (mathematical) induction'''.

items.title: Second Principle of Mathematical Induction/One-Based
items.statement:
Let $\map P n$ be a propositional function depending on $n \in \N_{>0}$.
Suppose that:
:$(1): \quad \map P 1$ is true
:$(2): \quad \forall k \in \N_{>0}: \map P 1 \land \map P 2 \land \ldots \land \map P {k - 1} \land \map P k \implies \map P {k + 1}$
Then:
:$\map P n$ is true for all $n \in \N_{>0}$.

items.title: Second Translation Property of Laplace Transforms
items.statement:
Let $g$ be the function defined as:
:$\map g t = \begin {cases} \map f {t - a} & : t > a \\ 0 & : t \le a \end {cases}$
Then:
:$\laptrans {\map g t} = e^{-a s} \map F s$

items.title: Self-Distributive Law for Conditional
Self-Distributive Law for Conditional/Formulation 1
items.statement: :$p \implies \paren {q \implies r} \dashv \vdash \paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r}$

items.title: Self-Distributive Law for Conditional/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} } \iff \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r} }$

items.title: Self-Distributive Law for Conditional/Formulation 2/Forward Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} } \implies \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r} }$

items.title: Self-Distributive Law for Conditional/Formulation 2/Reverse Implication
items.statement: :$\vdash \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r} } \implies \paren {p \implies \paren {q \implies r} }$

items.title: Semigroup is Group Iff Latin Square Property Holds
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup.
Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group {{iff}} for all $a, b \in S$ the Latin square property holds in $S$:
:$a \circ x = b$
:$y \circ a = b$
for $x$ and $y$ each unique in $S$.

items.title: Separable Discrete Space is Countable
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space.
Let $T$ be separable.
Then $S$ is countable.

items.title: Separable Metacompact Space is Lindelöf
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a separable topological space which is also metacompact.
Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

items.title: Sequence of P-adic Integers has Convergent Subsequence
items.statement:
Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p$.
Let $\sequence{x_n}$ be a sequence of $p$-adic integers.
Then:
:there exists a convergent subsequence $\sequence {x_{n_r} }_{r \mathop \in \N}$ of $\sequence{x_n}$

items.title: Sequence of Powers of Number less than One
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R$.
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as $x_n = x^n$.
Then:
:$\size x < 1$ {{iff}} $\sequence {x_n}$ is a null sequence.

items.title: Sequence of Powers of Number less than One/Necessary Condition
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R$ be such that $\size{x} < 1$.
Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as $x_n = x^n$.
Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is a null sequence.

items.title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Compact
items.statement: A sequentially compact metric space is compact.

items.title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Totally Bounded
items.statement:
Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space.
Let $M$ be sequentially compact.
Then $M$ is totally bounded.

items.title: Sequentially Compact Space is Countably Compact
items.statement: A sequentially compact topological space is also countably compact.

items.title: Set Complement inverts Subsets
items.statement: :$S \subseteq T \iff \map \complement T \subseteq \map \complement S$

items.title: Set Difference Intersection with First Set is Set Difference
items.statement: :$\paren {S \setminus T} \cap S = S \setminus T$

items.title: Set Difference Intersection with Second Set is Empty Set
items.statement: :$\paren {S \setminus T} \cap T = \O$

items.title: Set Difference Union Intersection
items.statement: :$S = \paren {S \setminus T} \cup \paren {S \cap T}$

items.title: Set Difference is Right Distributive over Set Intersection
items.statement: :$\paren {A \cap B} \setminus C = \paren {A \setminus C} \cap \paren {B \setminus C}$

items.title: Set Difference is Set
items.statement:
Let $x$ be a small class.
Let $A$ be a class.
Let $\map \MM B$ denote that $B$ is small.
Then: 
:$\map \MM {x \setminus A}$

items.title: Set Difference is Subset
items.statement: :$S \setminus T \subseteq S$

items.title: Set Difference with Intersection
items.statement: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.

items.title: Set Intersection Preserves Subsets
items.statement:
Let $A, B, S, T$ be sets.
Then:
:$A \subseteq B, \ S \subseteq T \implies A \cap S \subseteq B \cap T$

items.title: Set Intersection Preserves Subsets/Corollary
items.statement:
Let $A, B, S$ be sets.
Then:
:$A \subseteq B \implies A \cap S \subseteq B \cap S$

items.title: Set Union Preserves Subsets
items.statement:
Let $A, B, S, T$ be sets.
Then:
:$A \subseteq B, \ S \subseteq T \implies A \cup S \subseteq B \cup T$

items.title: Set between Connected Set and Closure is Connected
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space.
Let $H$ be a connected set of $T$.
Let $H \subseteq K \subseteq H^-$, where $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$. 
Then $K$ is connected.

items.title: Set is Closed iff Equals Topological Closure
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space.
Let $H \subseteq T$.
Then $H$ is closed in $T$ {{iff}}:
:$H = \map \cl H$

items.title: Set is Subset of Intersection of Supersets
items.statement:
Let $S$, $T_1$ and $T_2$ be sets.
Let $S$ be a subset of both $T_1$ and $T_2$.
Then:
:$S \subseteq T_1 \cap T_2$
That is:
:$\paren {S \subseteq T_1} \land \paren {S \subseteq T_2} \implies S \subseteq \paren {T_1 \cap T_2}$

items.title: Set is Subset of Union
items.statement:
The union of two sets is a superset of each:
:$S \subseteq S \cup T$
:$T \subseteq S \cup T$

items.title: Set is Subset of Union/Family of Sets
items.statement:
Let $\family {S_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of sets indexed by $I$.
Then:
:$\ds \forall \beta \in I: S_\beta \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha$
where $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha$ is the union of $\family {S_\alpha}$.

items.title: Set of Finite Character with Countable Union is Type M
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of sets of finite character.
Let its union $\bigcup S$ be countable.
Then $S$ is of type $M$.
That is:
:every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

items.title: Set of Finite Subsets of Countable Set is Countable
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a countable set.
Then the set of finite subsets of $A$ is countable.

items.title: Set of Integers Bounded Above by Integer has Greatest Element
items.statement:
Let $\Z$ be the set of integers.
Let $\le$ be the ordering on the integers.
Let $\O \subset S \subseteq \Z$ such that $S$ is bounded above in $\struct {\Z, \le}$.
Then $S$ has a greatest element.

items.title: Set of Prime Numbers is Infinite
items.statement: The number of primes is infinite.

items.title: Set of Subgroups forms Complete Lattice
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$.
Then:
:$\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.
where for every set $\mathbb H$ of subgroups of $G$:
:the infimum of $\mathbb H$ necessarily admitted by $\mathbb H$ is $\ds \bigcap \mathbb H$.

items.title: Simple Infinite Continued Fraction is Uniquely Determined by Limit
items.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 0}$ and $\sequence {b_n}_{n \mathop \ge 0}$ be simple infinite continued fractions in $\R$.
Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 0}$ and $\sequence {b_n}_{n \mathop \ge 0}$ have the same limit.
Then they are equal.

items.title: Sine Function is Absolutely Convergent
items.statement: The real sine function $\sin: \R \to \R$ is absolutely convergent.

items.title: Sine Function is Absolutely Convergent/Complex Case
items.statement: The complex sine function $\sin: \C \to \C$ is absolutely convergent.

items.title: Sine Function is Odd
items.statement:
:$\map \sin {-z} = -\sin z$
That is, the sine function is odd.

items.title: Sine Inequality
items.statement:
:$\size {\sin x} \le \size x$
for all $x \in \R$.

items.title: Sine and Cosine are Periodic on Reals
items.statement: The real sine function and real cosine function are periodic on the set of real numbers $\R$:

items.title: Sine and Cosine are Periodic on Reals/Pi
items.statement:
The real number $\pi$ (called '''pi''', pronounced '''pie''') is uniquely defined as:
:$\pi := \dfrac p 2$
where $p \in \R$ is the period of $\sin$ and $\cos$.

items.title: Sine and Cosine are Periodic on Reals/Sine
items.statement:
The real sine function is periodic
with the same period as the real cosine function.

items.title: Sine of 15 Degrees
items.statement: :$\sin 15 \degrees = \sin \dfrac \pi {12} = \dfrac {\sqrt 6 - \sqrt 2} 4$

items.title: Sine of 240 Degrees
items.statement: :$\sin 240 \degrees = \sin \dfrac {4 \pi} 3 = -\dfrac {\sqrt 3} 2$

items.title: Sine of 45 Degrees
items.statement: :$\sin 45 \degrees = \sin \dfrac \pi 4 = \dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2$

items.title: Sine of 75 Degrees
items.statement: :$\sin 75 \degrees = \sin \dfrac {5 \pi} {12} = \dfrac {\sqrt 6 + \sqrt 2} 4$

items.title: Sine of Complement equals Cosine
items.statement: :$\map \sin {\dfrac \pi 2 - \theta} = \cos \theta$

items.title: Sine of Complex Number
items.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers.
Let $i$ be the imaginary unit.
Then:
:$\sin \paren {a + b i} = \sin a \cosh b + i \cos a \sinh b$
where:
:$\sin$ denotes the sine function (real and complex)
:$\cos$ denotes the real cosine function
:$\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function
:$\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function.

items.title: Sine of Multiple of Pi by 2 plus i by Natural Logarithm of Golden Mean
items.statement:
Let $z = \dfrac \pi 2 + i \ln \phi$.
Then:
:$\dfrac {\sin n z} {\sin z} = i^{1 - n} F_n$
where:
:$\phi$ denotes the golden mean
:$F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number.

items.title: Sine of Sum
items.statement: :$\map \sin {a + b} = \sin a \cos b + \cos a \sin b$

items.title: Sine of i
items.statement: :$\sin i = \paren {\dfrac e 2 - \dfrac 1 {2 e} } i$

items.title: Singleton Set in Discrete Space is Compact
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $\tau$ is the discrete topology on $S$.
Let $x \in S$.
Then $\set x$ is compact.

items.title: Singleton of Element is Subset
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\set x$ be the singleton of $x$.
Then:
:$x \in S \iff \set x \subseteq S$

items.title: Size of Linearly Independent Subset is at Most Size of Finite Generator
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a division ring.
Let $V$ be an $R$-vector space.
Let $F \subseteq V$ be a finite generator of $V$ over $R$.
Let $L \subseteq V$ be linearly independent over $R$.
Then:
:$\size L \le \size F$

items.title: Skewness of Gamma Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution.
Then the skewness $\gamma_1$ of $X$ is given by:
:$\gamma_1 = \dfrac 2 {\sqrt \alpha}$

items.title: Skewness of Normal Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with a normal distribution with parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ for some $\mu \in \R$ and $\sigma \in \R_{> 0}$. 
Then the skewness $\gamma_1$ of $X$ is equal to $0$.

items.title: Slope of Tangent to Cycloid
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations:
:$x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$
:$y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$
The slope of the tangent to $C$ at the point $\tuple {x, y}$ is given by:
:$\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \cot \dfrac \theta 2$

items.title: Smallest Multiple of 9 with all Digits Even
items.statement: $288$ is the smallest integer multiple of $9$ all of whose digits are even.

items.title: Smallest Positive Integer Combination is Greatest Common Divisor
items.statement:
Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers.
Let $d \in \Z_{>0}$ be the smallest positive integer such that:
: $d = a s + b t$
where $s, t \in \Z$.
Then:
:$(1): \quad d \divides a \land d \divides b$
:$(2): \quad c \divides a \land c \divides b \implies c \divides d$
where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.
That is, $d$ is the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$.

items.title: Smullyan's Drinking Principle
items.statement:
Suppose that there is at least one person in the pub.
Then there is a person $x$ in the pub such that if $x$ is drinking, then everyone in the pub is drinking.

items.title: Solution by Integrating Factor/Examples/y' - 3y = sin x
items.statement:
The linear first order ODE:
:$\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - 3 y = \sin x$
has the general solution:
:$y = \dfrac 1 {10} \paren {3 \sin x - \cos x} + C e^{3 x}$

items.title: Solution to Linear First Order ODE with Constant Coefficients
items.statement:
A linear first order ODE with constant coefficients in the form:
:$(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + a y = \map Q x$
has the general solution:
:$\ds y = e^{-a x} \paren {\int e^{a x} \map Q x \rd x + C}$

items.title: Solution to Linear First Order Ordinary Differential Equation
items.statement:
A linear first order ordinary differential equation in the form:
:$\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map P x y = \map Q x$
has the general solution:
:$\ds y = e^{-\int P \rd x} \paren {\int Q e^{\int P \rd x} \rd x + C}$

items.title: Solutions of Pythagorean Equation/Primitive
items.statement:
The set of all primitive Pythagorean triples is generated by:
:$\tuple {2 m n, m^2 - n^2, m^2 + n^2}$
where:
:$m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ are (strictly) positive integers
:$m \perp n$, that is, $m$ and $n$ are coprime
:$m$ and $n$ are of opposite parity
:$m > n$

items.title: Spectrum of Self-Adjoint Bounded Linear Operator is Real
items.statement:
Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. 
Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded self-adjoint operator.
Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$.
Then:
:$\map \sigma T \subseteq \R$

items.title: Speed of Body under Free Fall from Height
items.statement:
Let an object $B$ be released above ground from a point near the Earth's surface and allowed to fall freely.
Let $B$ fall a distance $s$.
Then:
:$v = \sqrt {2 g s}$
where:
:$v$ is the speed of $B$ after having fallen a distance $s$
:$g$ is the Acceleration Due to Gravity at the height through which $B$ falls.
It is supposed that the distance $s$ is small enough that $g$ can be considered constant throughout.

items.title: Spherical Law of Cosines
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$.
Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively.
Then:
:$\cos a = \cos b \cos c + \sin b \sin c \cos A$

items.title: Spherical Law of Sines
items.statement:
Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$.
Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively.
Then:
:$\dfrac {\sin a} {\sin A} = \dfrac {\sin b} {\sin B} = \dfrac {\sin c} {\sin C}$

items.title: Square Matrix is Row Equivalent to Triangular Matrix
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$ over a commutative ring $R$.
Then $\mathbf A$ can be converted to an upper or lower triangular matrix by elementary row operations.

items.title: Square Matrix with Duplicate Rows has Zero Determinant
items.statement: If two rows of a square matrix over a commutative ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are the same, then its determinant is zero.

items.title: Square Root of 2 is Irrational
items.statement: :$\sqrt 2$ is irrational.

items.title: Square Root of Complex Number in Cartesian Form
Square Root of Number Minus Square Root
items.statement: :$\ds \sqrt {a - \sqrt b} = \sqrt {\dfrac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2} - \sqrt {\dfrac {a - \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2}$

items.title: Square Root of Number Plus Square Root
items.statement: :$\ds \sqrt {a + \sqrt b} = \sqrt {\dfrac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2} + \sqrt {\dfrac {a - \sqrt {a^2 - b} } 2}$

items.title: Square Root of Prime is Irrational
items.statement: The square root of a prime number is irrational.

items.title: Square Root of Sum as Sum of Square Roots
items.statement:
Let $a, b \in \R, a \ge b$.
Then:
:$\sqrt {a + b} = \sqrt {\dfrac a 2 + \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} 2} + \sqrt {\dfrac a 2 - \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} 2}$

items.title: Square of Cube Number is Cube
items.statement:
Let $a \in \N$ be a natural number.
Let $a$ be a cube number.
Then $a^2$ is also a cube number.
{{:Euclid:Proposition/IX/3}}

items.title: Square of Difference
items.statement: :$\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x - y}^2 = x^2 - 2 x y + y^2$

items.title: Square of Sum
items.statement: :$\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x + y}^2 = x^2 + 2 x y + y^2$

items.title: Square of Sum less Square
items.statement: :$\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {2x + y} y = \paren {x + y}^2 - x^2$

items.title: Square of Sum with Double
items.statement: :$\forall a, b \in \R: \paren {a + 2 b}^2 = a^2 + 4 a b + 4 b^2$

items.title: Square of Triangular Number equals Sum of Sequence of Cubes
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i^3 = {T_n}^2$
where $T_n$ denotes the $n$th triangular number.

items.title: Squeeze Theorem/Functions
items.statement:
Let $a$ be a point on an open real interval $I$.
Let $f$, $g$ and $h$ be real functions defined at all points of $I$ except for possibly at point $a$.
Suppose that:
:$\forall x \ne a \in I: \map g x \le \map f x \le \map h x$
:$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a} \map g x = \lim_{x \mathop \to a} \map h x = L$
Then:
:$\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a} \ \map f x = L$

items.title: Steiner-Lehmus Theorem
items.statement:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle.
Denote the lengths of the angle bisectors through the vertices $A$ and $B$ by $\omega_\alpha$ and $\omega_\beta$.
Let $\omega_\alpha = \omega_\beta$.
Then $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle.
:250px

items.title: Stirling's Formula
items.statement:
The factorial function can be approximated by the formula:
:$n! \sim \sqrt {2 \pi n} \paren {\dfrac n e}^n$
where $\sim$ denotes asymptotically equal.

items.title: Stirling's Formula/Refinement
items.statement:
A refinement of Stirling's Formula is:
:$n! = \sqrt {2 \pi n} \paren {\dfrac n e}^n \paren {1 + \dfrac 1 {12 n} + \map \OO  {\dfrac 1 {n^2} } }$

items.title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of Number with Greater
items.statement:
Let $\ds {n \brace k}$ denote a Stirling number of the second kind.
Then:
:$\ds {n \brace k} = 0$

items.title: Strict Lower Closure is Lower Section
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set.
Let $p \in S$.
Let $p^\prec$ denote the strict lower closure of $p$.
Then $p^\prec$ is a lower section.

items.title: Subgroup equals Conjugate iff Normal
items.statement:
:$\forall g \in G: g \circ N \circ g^{-1} = N$
:$\forall g \in G: g^{-1} \circ N \circ g = N$

items.title: Subgroup of Cyclic Group is Cyclic
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a cyclic group.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.
Then $H$ is cyclic.

items.title: Subgroup of Solvable Group is Solvable
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a solvable group.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.
Then $H$ is solvable.

items.title: Subset Product of Subgroups
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$.
Then $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ {{iff}} $H$ and $K$ are permutable.
That is:
$H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ {{iff}}:
:$H \circ K = K \circ H$
where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

items.title: Subset Product of Subgroups/Necessary Condition
items.statement:
Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be a group.
Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$.
Let $H \circ K$ be a subgroup of $G$.
Then $H$ and $K$ are permutable.
That is:
:$H \circ K = K \circ H$
where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

items.title: Subset Product of Subgroups/Sufficient Condition
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$.
Let $H$ and $K$ be permutable subgroups of $G$.
That is, suppose:
:$H \circ K = K \circ H$
where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.
Then $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$.

items.title: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup is Subgroup
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$.
Let:
:$(1): \quad H$ be a subgroup of $G$
:$(2): \quad N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$.
Let $H N$ denote subset product.
Then $H N$ and $N H$ are both subgroups of $G$.

items.title: Subset Relation is Transitive
items.statement:
The subset relation is transitive:
:$\paren {R \subseteq S} \land \paren {S \subseteq T} \implies R \subseteq T$

items.title: Subset equals Image of Preimage implies Surjection
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let:
:$\forall B \subseteq T: B = \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B$
where $f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$.
Then $f$ is a surjection.

items.title: Subset equals Preimage of Image implies Injection
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$.
Similarly, let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$.
Let:
:$\forall A \in \powerset S: A = \map {\paren {f^\gets \circ f^\to} } A$
Then $f$ is an injection.

items.title: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Successor
items.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$.
Let $x \in y$.
Then:
:$x^+ \in y^+$

items.title: Subset of Codomain is Superset of Image of Preimage
items.statement:
Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping.
Then:
:$B \subseteq T \implies \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B \subseteq B$
where:
:$f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$
:$f^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $f$
:$f \circ f^{-1}$ denotes composition of $f$ and $f^{-1}$.
This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as:
:$\forall B \in \powerset T: \map {\paren {f^\to \circ f^\gets} } B \subseteq B$

items.title: Subset of Well-Ordered Set is Well-Ordered
items.statement:
Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set.
Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$.
Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$.
Then the relational structure $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ is a well-ordered set.

items.title: Subspace of Product Space is Homeomorphic to Factor Space
items.statement:
Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set.
Let $\ds \struct {X, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \struct {X_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$.
Suppose that $X$ is non-empty.
Then for each $i \in I$ there is a subspace $Y_i \subseteq X$ which is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_i, \tau_i}$.
Specifically, for any $z \in X$, let:
:$Y_i = \set {x \in X: \forall j \in I \setminus \set i: x_j = z_j}$
and let $\upsilon_i$ be the subspace topology of $Y_i$ relative to $\tau$.
Then $\struct {Y_i, \upsilon_i}$ is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_i, \tau_i}$, where the homeomorphism is the restriction of the projection $\pr_i$ to $Y_i$.

items.title: Subspace of Product Space is Homeomorphic to Factor Space/Product with Singleton
items.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be non-empty topological spaces.
Let $b \in T_2$.
Let $T_1 \times T_2$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$.
Let $T_2 \times T_1$ be the product space of $T_2$ and $T_1$.
Then:
:$T_1$ is homeomorphic to the subspace $T_1 \times \set b$ of $T_1 \times T_2$
:$T_1$ is homeomorphic to the subspace $\set b \times T_1$ of $T_2 \times T_1$

items.title: Subspaces of Dimension 2 Real Vector Space
items.statement:
Take the $\R$-vector space $\left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$.
Let $S$ be a subspace of $\left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$.
Then $S$ is one of:
: $(1): \quad \left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$
: $(2): \quad \left\{{0}\right\}$
: $(3): \quad$ A line through the origin.

items.title: Subtraction of Divisors obeys Distributive Law
Subtraction of Multiples of Divisors obeys Distributive Law
Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers is Progressing
items.statement:
Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers as defined by the von Neumann construction.
Let $s: \omega \to \omega$ denote the successor mapping on $\omega$.
Then $s$ is a progressing mapping.

items.title: Successor Set of Ordinal is Ordinal
items.statement:
Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals.
Let $\alpha \in \On$ be an ordinal.
Then its successor set $\alpha^+ = \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ is also an ordinal.

items.title: Successor is Less than Successor
items.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$.
Then, $x \in y \iff x^+ \in y^+$.

items.title: Successor is Less than Successor/Sufficient Condition
items.statement:
== Proof 1 ==
{{:Successor is Less than Successor/Sufficient Condition/Proof 1}}

items.title: Sum Rule for Derivatives
items.statement:
Let $\map f x, \map j x, \map k x$ be real functions defined on the open interval $I$.
Let $\xi \in I$ be a point in $I$ at which both $j$ and $k$ are differentiable.
Let $\map f x = \map j x + \map k x$.
Then $f$ is differentiable at $\xi$ and:
:$\map {f'} \xi = \map {j'} \xi + \map {k'} \xi$
It follows from the definition of derivative that if $j$ and $k$ are both differentiable on the interval $I$, then:
:$\forall x \in I: \map {f'} x = \map {j'} x + \map {k'} x$

items.title: Sum from 1 to n of 1 over r(r+1)
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{r \mathop = 1}^n \frac 1 {r \paren {r + 1} } = \frac n {n + 1}$

items.title: Sum of Angles of Triangle equals Two Right Angles
items.statement:
In a triangle, the sum of the three interior angles equals two right angles.
{{:Euclid:Proposition/I/32}}

items.title: Sum of Arcsine and Arccosine
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $-1 \le x \le 1$.
Then:
:$\arcsin x + \arccos x = \dfrac \pi 2$
where $\arcsin$ and $\arccos$ denote arcsine and arccosine respectively.

items.title: Sum of Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence
items.statement:
Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as:
:$a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$
Then its closed-form expression is:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + \frac {r d \paren {1 - n r^{n - 1} + \paren {n - 1} r^n} } {\paren {1 - r}^2}$

items.title: Sum of Arithmetic Sequence
Sum of Bernoulli Numbers by Power of Two and Binomial Coefficient
Sum of Binomial Coefficients over Lower Index
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \binom n i = 2^n$

items.title: Sum of Cube Roots of Unity
items.statement:
Let $U_3 = \set {1, \omega, \omega^2}$ denote the Cube Roots of Unity.
Then:
:$1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0$

items.title: Sum of Cubes of Three Indeterminates Minus 3 Times their Product
items.statement:
For indeterminates $x, y, z$:
:$x^3 + y^3 + z^3 - 3 x y z = \paren {x + y + z} \paren {x + \omega y + \omega^2 z} \paren {x + \omega^2 y + \omega z}$
where $\omega = -\dfrac 1 2 + \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 2$

items.title: Sum of Entries in Row of Pascal's Triangle
items.statement: The sum of all the entries in the $n$th row of Pascal's triangle is equal to $2^n$.

items.title: Sum of Even Index Binomial Coefficients
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} \binom n {2 i} = 2^{n - 1}$

items.title: Sum of Even Integers is Even
items.statement: The sum of any finite number of even integers is itself even.

items.title: Sum of Expectations of Independent Trials
items.statement:
Let $\EE_1, \EE_2, \ldots, \EE_n$ be a sequence of experiments whose outcomes are independent of each other.
Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be discrete random variables on $\EE_1, \EE_2, \ldots, \EE_n$ respectively.
Let $\expect {X_j}$ denote the expectation of $X_j$ for $j \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$.
Then we have, whenever both sides are defined:
:$\ds \expect {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n X_j} = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \expect {X_j}$
That is, the sum of the expectations equals the expectation of the sum.

items.title: Sum of Fourth Powers of Sine and Cosine
items.statement: :$\cos^4 x + \sin^4 x = 1 - 2 \cos^2 x \sin^2 x$

items.title: Sum of Geometric Sequence
items.statement:
Let $x$ be an element of one of the standard number fields: $\Q, \R, \C$ such that $x \ne 1$.
Let $n \in \N_{>0}$.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} x^j = \frac {x^n - 1} {x - 1}$

items.title: Sum of Infinite Geometric Sequence
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a standard number field, that is $\Q$, $\R$ or $\C$.
Let $z \in S$.
Let $\size z < 1$, where $\size z$ denotes:
:the absolute value of $z$, for real and rational $z$
:the complex modulus of $z$ for complex $z$.
Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty z^n$ converges absolutely to $\dfrac 1 {1 - z}$.

items.title: Sum of Integrals on Adjacent Intervals for Integrable Functions
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a real function which is Darboux integrable on any closed interval $\mathbb I$.
Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb I$.
Then:
:$\ds \int_a^c \map f t \rd t + \int_c^b \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t$

items.title: Sum of Integrals on Adjacent Intervals for Integrable Functions/Lemma
items.statement:
Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval.
Let $c$ be a real number.
Let $a < c < b$.
Let $f$ be a real function defined on $\closedint a b$.
Let $\map L S$ be the lower Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ where $S$ is a subdivision of $\closedint a b$.
Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite subdivisions of $\closedint a b$.
Let:
:$Q = P \cup \set c$.
Then:
:$\map L Q \ge \map L P$

items.title: Sum of Internal Angles of Polygon
items.statement: The sum $S$ of all internal angles of a polygon with $n$ sides is given by the formula $S = \paren {n - 2} 180 \degrees$.

items.title: Sum of Logarithms/General Logarithm
items.statement:
Let $x, y, b \in \R$ be strictly positive real numbers such that $b > 1$.
Then:
:$\log_b x + \log_b y = \map {\log_b} {x y}$
where $\log_b$ denotes the logarithm to base $b$.

items.title: Sum of Logarithms/Natural Logarithm
items.statement:
Let $x, y \in \R$ be strictly positive real numbers.
Then:
:$\ln x + \ln y = \map \ln {x y}$
where $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm.

items.title: Sum of Powers of 2
Sum of Reciprocals of Powers as Euler Product
items.statement:
Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function.
Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\sigma > 1$.
Then:
:$\ds \map \zeta s = \prod_{\text {$p$ prime} } \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} }$
where the infinite product runs over the prime numbers.

items.title: Sum of Reciprocals of Primes is Divergent
items.statement:
Let $n \in \N: n \ge 1$.
There exists a (strictly) positive real number $C \in \R_{>0}$ such that:
:$(1): \quad \ds \sum_{\substack {p \mathop \in \Bbb P \\ p \mathop \le n} } \frac 1 p > \map \ln {\ln n} - C$
where $\Bbb P$ is the set of all prime numbers.
:$(2): \quad \ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {\map \ln {\ln n} - C} = +\infty$

items.title: Sum of Reciprocals of Squares of Odd Integers as Double Integral
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {\paren {2 n - 1}^2} = \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \frac 1 {1 - x^2 y^2} \rd x \rd y$

items.title: Sum of Roots of Polynomial
items.statement:
Let $P$ be the polynomial equation:
: $a_n z^n + a_{n - 1} z^{n - 1} + \cdots + a_1 z + a_0 = 0$
such that $a_n \ne 0$.
The sum of the roots of $P$ is $-\dfrac {a_{n - 1} } {a_n}$.

items.title: Sum of Sequence as Summation of Difference of Adjacent Terms
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a strictly positive integer.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k = n a_n - \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^{n - 1} k \paren {a_{k + 1} - a_k}$

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Binomial Coefficients by Powers of 2
Sum of Sequence of Cubes
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i^3 = \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i}^2 = \frac {n^2 \paren {n + 1}^2} 4$

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Fourth Powers
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n k^4 = \dfrac {\paren {n + 1} n \paren {n + \frac 1 2} \paren {3 n^2 + 3 n - 1} } {15}$

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Harmonic Numbers
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k = \paren {n + 1} H_n - n$
where $H_k$ denotes the $k$th harmonic number.

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Odd Squares/Corollary
items.statement: :$\ds \forall n \in \N: \sum_{r \mathop = 0}^n \paren {2 r + 1}^2 = \frac {\paren {n + 1} \paren {2 n + 1} \paren {2 n + 3} } 3$

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Power by Index
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n j x^j = \frac {n x^{n + 2} - \paren {n + 1} x^{n + 1} + x} {\paren {x - 1}^2}$
for $x \ne 1$.

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Product of Fibonacci Number with Binomial Coefficient
Sum of Sequence of Squares
items.statement: :$\ds \forall n \in \N: \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i^2 = \frac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {2 n + 1} } 6$

items.title: Sum of Sequence of Triangular Numbers
Sum of Sequence of k x k!
Sum of Sequence of n Choose 2
Sum of Sequence of n by 2 to the Power of n
Sum of Squared Deviations from Mean
items.statement:
Let $S = \set {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ be a set of real numbers.
Let $\overline x$ denote the arithmetic mean of $S$.
Then: 
:$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x_i - \overline x}^2 = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren { {x_i}^2 - {\overline x}^2}$

items.title: Sum of Squares of Binomial Coefficients
Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
items.statement: :$\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1$

items.title: Sum of Squares of Sum and Difference
items.statement: :$\forall a, b \in \R: \paren {a + b}^2 + \paren {a - b}^2 = 2 \paren {a^2 + b^2}$

items.title: Sum of Summations equals Summation of Sum
items.statement:
Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers.
Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a summation over $R$.
Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{\map R i} \paren {b_i + c_i} = \sum_{\map R i} b_i + \sum_{\map R i} c_i$

items.title: Sum of Summations equals Summation of Sum/Infinite Sequence
items.statement:
Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers $\Z$.
Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a summation over $R$.
Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be infinite.
Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} b_i$ and $\ds \sum_{\map R i} c_i$ be convergent.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{\map R i} \paren {b_i + c_i} = \sum_{\map R i} b_i + \sum_{\map R i} c_i$

items.title: Sum of Two Odd Powers
Sum of Two Odd Powers/Examples/Sum of Two Cubes
items.statement: :$x^3 + y^3 = \paren {x + y} \paren {x^2 - x y + y^2}$

items.title: Sum of nth Fibonacci Number over nth Power of 2
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {F_n} {2^n} = 2$
where $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number.

items.title: Sum over k of n+k Choose 2 k by 2 k Choose k by -1^k over k+1
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_k \binom {n + k} {2 k} \binom {2 k} k \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {k + 1} = \sqbrk {n = 0}$

items.title: Sum over k of n+k Choose m+2k by 2k Choose k by -1^k over k+1
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_k \binom {n + k} {m + 2 k} \binom {2 k} k \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {k + 1} = \binom {n - 1} {m - 1}$

items.title: Sum over k of r-kt Choose k by r over r-kt by s-(n-k)t Choose n-k by s over s-(n-k)t
items.statement:
For $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$:
:$\ds \sum_k \map {A_k} {r, t} \map {A_{n - k} } {s, t} = \map {A_n} {r + s, t}$
where $\map {A_n} {x, t}$ is the polynomial of degree $n$ defined as:
:$\map {A_n} {x, t} = \dbinom {x - n t} n \dfrac x {x - n t}$
where $x \ne n t$.

items.title: Sum over k of r-kt choose k by z^k
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a non-negative integer.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_k \dbinom {r - t k} k z^k = \frac {x^{r + 1} } {\paren {t + 1} x - t}$
where $\dbinom {r - t k} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

items.title: Sum over k of r-tk Choose k by s-t(n-k) Choose n-k by r over r-tk
items.statement:
Let $r, s, t \in \R, n \in \Z$.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} \binom {r - t k} k \binom {s - t \paren {n - k} } {n - k} \frac r {r - t k} = \binom {r + s - t n} n$

items.title: Sum over k of r Choose k by -1^r-k by Polynomial
items.statement:
Let $r \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.
Then:
:$\ds \sum_k \binom r k \paren {-1}^{r - k} \map {P_r} k = r! \, b_r$
where:
:$\map {P_r} k = b_0 + b_1 k + \cdots + b_r k^r$ is a polynomial in $k$ of degree $r$.

items.title: Summation Formula for Reciprocal of Binomial Coefficient
Summation of Powers over Product of Differences
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \begin{pmatrix} {\dfrac { {x_j}^r} {\ds \prod_{\substack {1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n \\ k \mathop \ne j} } \paren {x_j - x_k} } } \end{pmatrix} = \begin{cases} 0 & : 0 \le r < n - 1 \\ 1 & : r = n - 1 \\ \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n x_j & : r = n \end{cases}$

items.title: Summation of Products of n Numbers taken m at a time with Repetitions
Summation of Products of n Numbers taken m at a time with Repetitions/Examples/Order 2
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \sum_{j \mathop = a}^i x_i x_j = \dfrac 1 2 \paren {\paren {\sum_{i \mathop = a}^b x_i}^2 + \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = a}^b {x_i}^2} }$

items.title: Summation of Products of n Numbers taken m at a time with Repetitions/Examples/Order 3
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \sum_{j \mathop = a}^i \sum_{k \mathop = a}^j x_i x_j x_k = \dfrac { {S_1}^3} 6 + \dfrac {S_1 S_2} 2 + \dfrac {S_3} 3$
where:
:$\ds S_r := \sum_{k \mathop = a}^b {x_k}^r$

items.title: Summation of i from 1 to n of Summation of j from 1 to i
items.statement: :$\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^i a_{i j} = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{i \mathop = j}^n a_{i j}$

items.title: Summation to n of Power of k over k
items.statement:
:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {x^k} k = H_n + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dbinom n k \dfrac {\paren {x - 1}^k} k$
where:
:$H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number
:$\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

items.title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real-Valued Functions is Metric
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a set.
Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real-valued functions $f: X \to \R$.
Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$.
Then $d$ is a metric.

items.title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real Functions on Closed Interval is Metric
items.statement:
Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval.
Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$.
Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$.
Then $d$ is a metric.

items.title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real Sequences is Metric
items.statement:
Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real sequences.
Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$.
Then $d$ is a metric.

items.title: Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions is Metric
items.statement:
Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval.
Let $\mathscr C \closedint a b$ be the set of all continuous functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$.
Let $d$ be the supremum metric on  $\mathscr C \closedint a b$.
Then $d$ is a metric.

items.title: Supremum of Set of Real Numbers is at least Supremum of Subset
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of real numbers.
Let $S$ have a supremum.
Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$.
Then $\sup T$ exists and:
:$\sup T \le \sup S$

items.title: Supremum of Subset
items.statement:
Let $\left({U, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set.
Let $S \subseteq U$.
Let $T \subseteq S$.
Let $S$ admit a supremum (in $U$).
If $T$ also admits a supremum (in $U$), then $\sup \left({T}\right) \preceq\sup \left({S}\right)$.

items.title: Surjection iff Epimorphism in Category of Sets
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets.
Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{Set}$, i.e. a mapping.
Then:
:$f$ is a surjection {{iff}} it is an epimorphism.

items.title: Surjection iff Right Cancellable
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a mapping.
Then $f$ is a surjection {{iff}} $f$ is right cancellable.

items.title: Surjection iff Right Cancellable/Necessary Condition
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a surjection.
Then $f$ is right cancellable.

items.title: Surjection iff Right Cancellable/Sufficient Condition
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a mapping which is right cancellable.
Then $f$ is a surjection.

items.title: Surjection iff Right Inverse
items.statement:
A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is a surjection {{iff}}:
:$\exists g: T \to S: f \circ g = I_T$
where:
:$g$ is a mapping
:$I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$.
That is, {{iff}} $f$ has a right inverse.

items.title: Sylow p-Subgroups of Group of Order 2p
items.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime.
Let $G$ be a group of order $2 p$.
Then $G$ has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup.
This Sylow $p$-subgroup is normal.

items.title: Symmetric Difference is Associative
items.statement:
Symmetric difference is associative:
:$R \symdif \paren {S \symdif T} = \paren {R \symdif S} \symdif T$

items.title: Symmetric Difference with Intersection forms Ring
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let:
:$\symdif$ denote the symmetric difference operation
:$\cap$ denote the set intersection operation
:$\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$.
Then $\struct {\powerset S, \symdif, \cap}$ is a commutative ring with unity, in which the unity is $S$.
This ring is not an integral domain.

items.title: Symmetric Group is Group
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\map \Gamma S$ denote the set of all permutations on $S$.
Then $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$, the symmetric group on $S$, forms a group.

items.title: Symmetric Group is not Abelian
items.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group of order $n$ where $n \ge 3$.
Then $S_n$ is not abelian.

items.title: Symmetric Groups of Same Order are Isomorphic
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer.
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be sets whose cardinality $\card {T_1}$ and $\card {T_2}$ are both $n$.
Let $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_1}, \circ}$ and $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_2}, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$ and $T$ respectively.
Then $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_1}, \circ}$ and $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_2}, \circ}$ are isomorphic.

items.title: Symmetric and Transitive Relation is not necessarily Reflexive
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Let $\alpha \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$.
Let $\alpha$ be both symmetric and transitive.
Then it is not necessarily the case that $\alpha$ is also reflexive.

items.title: Symmetry Rule for Binomial Coefficients
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{>0}, k \in \Z$.
Then:
:$\dbinom n k = \dbinom n {n - k}$

items.title: T0 Space is not necessarily T1
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a be a $T_0$ space.
Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

items.title: T3 Lindelöf Space is T4
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ Lindelöf topological space.
Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

items.title: T3 Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is T4 Space
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ topological space.
Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis.
Then:
:$T$ is a $T_4$ space

items.title: Tableau Extension Lemma/General Statement
items.statement:
Let $\mathbf H'$ be another finite set of WFFs.
Then there exists a finished finite propositional tableau $T'$ such that:
$(1):\quad$ the root of $T'$ is $\mathbf H \cup \mathbf H'$;
$(2):\quad$ $T$ is a rooted subtree of $T'$.

items.title: Tangent of 15 Degrees
items.statement: :$\tan 15^\circ = \tan \dfrac {\pi} {12} = 2 - \sqrt 3$

items.title: Tangent of 22.5 Degrees
items.statement: :$\tan 22.5 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 8 = \sqrt 2 - 1$

items.title: Tangent of Sum
items.statement: :$\map \tan {a + b} = \dfrac {\tan a + \tan b} {1 - \tan a \tan b}$

items.title: Tangent of Sum of Series of Angles
Tangent of Sum of Three Angles
items.statement: :$\map \tan {A + B + C} = \dfrac {\tan A + \tan B + \tan C - \tan A \tan B \tan C} {1 - \tan B \tan C - \tan C \tan A - \tan A \tan B}$

items.title: Tangent of i
items.statement: :$\tan i = \paren {\dfrac {e^2 - 1} {e^2 + 1} } i$

items.title: Tangent times Tangent plus Cotangent
items.statement: :$\tan x \paren {\tan x + \cot x} = \sec^2 x$

items.title: Tangent to Cycloid
items.statement:
Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations:
:$x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$
:$y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$
Then the tangent to $C$ at a point $\tuple {x, y}$ on $C$ is given by the equation:
:$y - a \paren {1 - \cos \theta} = \dfrac {\sin \theta} {1 - \cos \theta} \paren {x - a \theta + a \sin \theta}$

items.title: Tautological Antecedent
items.statement: :$\top \implies p \dashv \vdash p$

items.title: Tautological Consequent
items.statement: :$p \implies \top \dashv \vdash \top$

items.title: Tautology is Negation of Contradiction
items.statement:
A tautology implies and is implied by the negation of a contradiction:
:$\top \dashv \vdash \neg \bot$
That is, a truth can not be false, and a non-falsehood must be a truth.

items.title: Taxicab Metric is Metric
items.statement: The taxicab metric is a metric.

items.title: Taxicab Metric on Real Vector Space is Metric
items.statement: The taxicab metric on the real vector space $\R^n$ is a metric.

items.title: Taylor's Theorem
items.statement: Every infinitely differentiable function can be approximated by a series of polynomials.

items.title: Thales' Theorem
items.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two points on opposite ends of the diameter of a circle.
Let $C$ be another point on the circle such that $C \ne A, B$.
Then the lines $AC$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to each other.
:400px

items.title: There Exists No Universal Set
items.statement:
There exists no set which is an absolutely universal set.
That is:
:$\map \neg {\exists \, \UU: \forall T: T \in \UU}$
where $T$ is any arbitrary object at all.
That is, a set that contains ''everything'' cannot exist.

items.title: There exist no 4 Consecutive Triangular Numbers which are all Sphenic Numbers
items.statement:
Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number.
Let $T_n$, $T_{n + 1}$, $T_{n + 2}$, and $T_{n + 3}$ be the $n$th, $n + 1$th, $n + 2$th and $n + 3$th triangular numbers respectively.
Then it is not the case that all of $T_n$, $T_{n + 1}$, $T_{n + 2}$, and $T_{n + 3}$ are sphenic numbers.

items.title: Third Isomorphism Theorem/Groups
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, and let:
:$H, N$ be normal subgroups of $G$
:$N$ be a subset of $H$.
Then:
:$(1): \quad N$ is a normal subgroup of $H$
:$(2): \quad H / N$ is a normal subgroup of $G / N$
:::where $H / N$ denotes the quotient group of $H$ by $N$
:$(3): \quad \dfrac {G / N} {H / N} \cong \dfrac G H$
:::where $\cong$ denotes group isomorphism.

items.title: Third Sylow Theorem
items.statement: All the Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate.

items.title: Three times Number whose Divisor Sum is Square
items.statement:
Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer.
Let the divisor sum $\map {\sigma_1} n$ of $n$ be square.
Let $3$ not be a divisor of $n$.
Then the divisor sum of $3 n$ is square.

items.title: Topological Closure of Singleton is Irreducible
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $x$ be a point of $T$.
Then:
:$\set x^-$ is irreducible
where $\set x^-$ denotes the topological closure of $\set x$.

items.title: Topological Closure of Subset is Subset of Topological Closure
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $H \subseteq K$ and $K \subseteq S$.
Then:
:$\map \cl H \subseteq \map \cl K$
where $\map \cl H$ denotes the closure of $H$.

items.title: Topological Subspace is Topological Space
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $H \subseteq X$ be a non-empty subset of $X$.
Let $\tau_H = \set {U \cap H: U \in \tau}$ be the subspace topology on $H$.
Then the topological subspace $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ is a topological space.

items.title: Totally Bounded Metric Space is Second-Countable
items.statement:
Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space which is totally bounded.
Then $M$ is second-countable.

items.title: Tower Law for Subgroups
items.statement:
Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with finite index.
Let $K$ be a subgroup of $H$.
Then:
:$\index G K = \index G H \index H K$
where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$.

items.title: Transfinite Induction/Principle 1
items.statement:
Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals.
Let $A$ denote a class.
Suppose that:
:For all elements $x$ of $\On$, if $x$ is a subset of $A$, then $x$ is an element of $A$.
Then $\On \subseteq A$.

items.title: Transfinite Induction/Schema 1
items.statement:
Let $\map P x$ be a property 
Suppose that:
:If $\map P x$ holds for all ordinals $x$ less than $y$, then $\map P y$ also holds.
Then $\map P x$ holds for all ordinals $x$.

items.title: Transfinite Induction/Schema 2
items.statement:
Let $\map \phi x$ be a property satisfying the following conditions:
:$(1): \quad \map \phi \O$ is true
:$(2): \quad$ If $x$ is an ordinal, then $\map \phi x \implies \map \phi {x^+}$
:$(3): \quad$ If $y$ is a limit ordinal, then $\paren {\forall x < y: \map \phi x} \implies \map \phi y$
where $x^+$ denotes the successor of $x$.
Then, $\map \phi x$ is true for all ordinals $x$.

items.title: Translation of Closed Set in Topological Vector Space is Closed Set
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a topological field.
Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. 
Let $F$ be a closed set in $X$. 
Let $x \in X$.
Then $F + x$ is a closed set in $X$.

items.title: Triangle Inequality/Complex Numbers
items.statement:
Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers.
Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of $z$.
Then:
:$\cmod {z_1 + z_2} \le \cmod {z_1} + \cmod {z_2}$

items.title: Triangle Inequality/Real Numbers
items.statement:
Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers.
Let $\size x$ denote the absolute value of $x$.
Then:
:$\size {x + y} \le \size x + \size y$

items.title: Triangle Right-Angle-Hypotenuse-Side Congruence
items.statement:
If two right triangles have:
:their hypotenuses equal
:another of their respective sides equal
they will also have:
:their third sides equal
:the remaining two angles equal to their respective remaining angles.

items.title: Triangle Side-Side-Side Congruence
items.statement:
Let two triangles have all $3$ sides equal.
Then they also have all $3$ angles equal.
Thus two triangles whose sides are all equal are themselves congruent.
{{:Euclid:Proposition/I/8}}

items.title: Triangle with Two Equal Angles is Isosceles
Trichotomy Law for Real Numbers
Triple Angle Formulas/Cosine
items.statement: :$\cos 3 \theta = 4 \cos^3 \theta - 3 \cos \theta$

items.title: Triple Angle Formulas/Sine
items.statement: :$\sin 3 \theta = 3 \sin \theta - 4 \sin^3 \theta$

items.title: Triple Angle Formulas/Tangent
items.statement: :$\tan 3 \theta = \dfrac {3 \tan \theta - \tan^3 \theta} {1 - 3 \tan^2 \theta}$

items.title: True Statement is implied by Every Statement
True Statement is implied by Every Statement/Formulation 2
items.statement: :$\vdash q \implies \paren {p \implies q}$

items.title: Tuning Fork Delta Sequence
items.statement:
thumb300pxThe graph of the tuning fork delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the rectangles becomes thinner and longer. The area of each shape is equal to $1$, where the area under the axis contributes negatively. Note that at $x = 0$ the graph is always negative, and its value here approaches $-\infty$. Only taking the entire graph we can ensure the proper behaviour for $n$ approaching $\infty$,
Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a sequence such that:
:<nowiki>$\map {\delta_n} x := \begin {cases}
-n & : \size x < \dfrac 1 {2n} \\ \\
2n & : \dfrac 1 {2n} \le \size x \le \dfrac 1 n \\ \\
0 & : \size x > \dfrac 1 n \end {cases}$</nowiki>
Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a delta sequence.
That is, in the distributional sense it holds that:
:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {\delta_n} x = \map \delta x$
or
:$\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map {\delta_n} x \map \phi x \rd x = \map \delta \phi$
where:
:$\phi \in \map \DD \R$ is a test function
:$\delta$ is the Dirac delta distribution
:$\map \delta x$ is the abuse of notation, usually interpreted as an infinitely thin and tall spike with its area equal to $1$.

items.title: Tychonoff's Theorem
items.statement:
Let $I$ be an indexing set.
Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces.
Let $\ds X = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the corresponding product space.
Then $X$ is compact {{iff}} each $X_i$ is compact.

items.title: Ultrafilter Lemma
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a set.
Every filter on $S$ is contained in an ultrafilter on $S$.

items.title: Unbounded Set of Real Numbers is not Compact
items.statement:
Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers considered as a Euclidean space.
Let $S \subseteq \R$ be unbounded in $\R$.
Then $S$ is not a compact subspace of $\R$.

items.title: Unbounded Space Minus Bounded Space is Unbounded
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a metric space.
Let $A \subseteq M$ be unbounded in $M$.
Let $B \subseteq M$ be bounded in $M$.
Then $A \setminus B$ is unbounded in $M$.

items.title: Uncountable Excluded Point Space is not Second-Countable
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be an uncountable excluded point space.
Then $T$ is not second-countable.

items.title: Uniformly Continuous Function is Continuous/Real Function
items.statement:
Let $I$ be an interval of $\R$.
Let $f: I \to \R$ be a uniformly continuous real function on $I$.
Then $f$ is continuous on $I$.

items.title: Union Distributes over Intersection
items.statement:
Set union is distributive over set intersection:
:$R \cup \paren {S \cap T} = \paren {R \cup S} \cap \paren {R \cup T}$

items.title: Union from Synthetic Basis is Topology
items.statement:
Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis on a set $X$.
Let $\ds \tau = \set {\bigcup \AA: \AA \subseteq \BB}$.
Then $\tau$ is a topology on $X$.

items.title: Union from Synthetic Basis is Topology/Open Set Axiom 3
items.statement:
Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis on a set $X$.
Let $\ds \tau = \set {\bigcup \AA: \AA \subseteq \BB}$.
Then $\tau$ fulfils {{Open-set-axiom|3}}.

items.title: Union is Empty iff Sets are Empty
items.statement:
If the union of two sets is the empty set, then both are themselves empty:
:$S \cup T = \O \iff S = \O \land T = \O$

items.title: Union of Connected Sets with Common Point is Connected
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of connected sets of $T$.
Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$.
Then
:$\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a connected set of $T$.

items.title: Union of Connected Sets with Non-Empty Intersections is Connected
items.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.
Let $I$ be an indexing set.
Let $\AA = \family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of $S$, all connected in $T$.
Let $\AA$ be such that no two of its elements are disjoint:
:$\forall B, C \in \AA: B \cap C \ne \O$
Then $\ds \bigcup \AA$ is itself connected.

items.title: Union of Countable Sets of Sets
items.statement:
Let $\AA$ and $\BB$ be countable sets of sets.
Then:
:$\set {A \cup B: A \in \AA, B \in \BB}$
is also countable.

items.title: Union of Disjoint Singletons is Doubleton
items.statement:
Let $\set a$ and $\set b$ be singletons such that $a \ne b$.
Then:
:$\set a \cup \set b = \set {a, b}$

items.title: Union of Equivalences
items.statement: The union of two equivalence relations is '''not''' necessarily an equivalence relation itself.

items.title: Union of Finite Sets is Finite
items.statement:
Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets.
Then $S \cup T$ is a finite set.

items.title: Union of Initial Segments is Initial Segment or All of Woset
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered non-empty set.
Let $A \subseteq X$.
Let:
:$\ds J = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} S_x$
be a union of initial segments defined by the elements of $A$.
Then either:
:$J = X$
or:
:$J$ is an initial segment of $X$.

items.title: Union of Set of Ordinals is Ordinal
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of ordinals.
Then $\bigcup A$ is an ordinal.

items.title: Union of Subsets is Subset
items.statement:
Let $S_1$, $S_2$, and $T$ be sets.
Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ both be subsets of $T$.
Then:
:$S_1 \cup S_2 \subseteq T$
That is:
:$\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \implies \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

items.title: Union of Transitive Class is Transitive
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a class.
Let $\bigcup A$ denote the union of $A$.
Let $A$ be transitive.
Then $\bigcup A$ is also transitive.

items.title: Union with Empty Set
items.statement:
The union of any set with the empty set is the set itself:
:$S \cup \O = S$

items.title: Union with Superset is Superset
items.statement: :$S \subseteq T \iff S \cup T = T$

items.title: Uniqueness of Measures
items.statement:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space.
Let $\GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be a generator for $\Sigma$; that is, $\Sigma = \map \sigma \GG$.
Suppose that $\GG$ satisfies the following conditions:
:$(1):\quad \forall G, H \in \GG: G \cap H \in \GG$
:$(2):\quad$ There exists an exhausting sequence $\sequence {G_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \uparrow X$ in $\GG$
Let $\mu, \nu$ be measures on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$, and suppose that:
:$(3):\quad \forall G \in \GG: \map \mu G = \map \nu G$
:$(4):\quad \forall n \in \N: \map \mu {G_n}$ is finite
Then:
:$\mu = \nu$

items.title: Uniqueness of Positive Root of Positive Real Number/Positive Exponent
items.statement:
Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$.
Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 0$.
Then there is at most one $y \in \R: y \ge 0$ such that $y^n = x$.

items.title: Units of Gaussian Integers
items.statement:
Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ be the ring of Gaussian integers.
The set of units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ is $\set {1, i, -1, -i}$.

items.title: Units of Gaussian Integers form Group
items.statement:
Let $U_\C$ be the set of units of the Gaussian integers:
:$U_\C = \set {1, i, -1, -i}$
where $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i = \sqrt {-1}$.
Let $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ be the algebraic structure formed by $U_\C$ under the operation of complex multiplication.
Then $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ forms a cyclic group under complex multiplication.

items.title: Unity Divides All Elements
items.statement:
Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose unity is $1_D$.
Then unity is a divisor of every element of $D$:
:$\forall x \in D: 1_D \divides x$
Also:
:$\forall x \in D: -1_D \divides x$

items.title: Unity is Unit
items.statement: The unity in a ring is a unit.

items.title: Universal Class is Proper
items.statement:
Let $V$ denote the universal class.
Then $V$ is a proper class.

items.title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of Number with Greater
items.statement:
Let $\ds {n \brack k}$ denote an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind.
Then:
:$\ds {n \brack k} = 0$

items.title: Upper Bound of Natural Logarithm
items.statement:
Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$ where $x \in \R_{>0}$.
Then:
:$\ln x \le x - 1$

items.title: Value of Cauchy Determinant
items.statement:
Let $D_n$ be a Cauchy determinant of order $n$:
:<nowiki>$\begin{vmatrix}
\dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_n} \\
\dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_n} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
\dfrac 1 {x_n + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_n + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_n + y_n} \\
\end{vmatrix}$</nowiki>
Then the value of $D_n$ is given by:
:$D_n = \dfrac {\ds \prod_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_j - x_i} \paren {y_j - y_i} } {\ds \prod_{1 \mathop \le i, \, j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_i + y_j} }$
Let $D_n$ be given by:
:<nowiki>$\begin {vmatrix}
\dfrac 1 {x_1 - y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_1 - y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_1 - y_n} \\
\dfrac 1 {x_2 - y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_2 - y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_2 - y_n} \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
\dfrac 1 {x_n - y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_n - y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_n - y_n} \\
\end {vmatrix}$</nowiki>
Then its determinant is given by:
:$D_n = \dfrac {\ds \prod_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_j - x_i} \paren {y_i - y_j} } {\ds \prod_{1 \mathop \le i, \, j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_i - y_j} }$

items.title: Value of Vacuum Permeability
items.statement:
The value of the '''vacuum permeability''' is calculated as:
:$\mu_0 = 1 \cdotp 25663 \, 70621 \, 2 (19) \times 10^{-6} \, \mathrm H \, \mathrm m^{-1}$ (henries per metre)
with a relative uncertainty of $1 \cdotp 5 \times 10^{-10}$.

items.title: Value of Vacuum Permittivity
items.statement:
The value of the '''vacuum permittivity''' is calculated as:
:$\varepsilon_0 = 8 \cdotp 85418 \, 78128 (13) \times 10^{-12} \, \mathrm F \, \mathrm m^{-1}$ (farads per metre)
with a relative uncertainty of $1 \cdotp 5 \times 10^{-10}$.

items.title: Value of Vandermonde Determinant/Formulation 1
items.statement:
Let $V_n$ be the '''Vandermonde determinant of order $n$''' defined as the following formulation:
{{:Definition:Vandermonde Determinant/Formulation 1}}
Its value is given by:
:$\ds V_n = \prod_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_j - x_i}$

items.title: Variance of Bernoulli Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Bernoulli distribution with parameter $p$:
:$X \sim \Bernoulli p$
Then the variance of $X$ is given by:
:$\var X = p \paren {1 - p}$

items.title: Variance of Beta Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X \sim \BetaDist \alpha \beta$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\operatorname {Beta}$ denotes the beta distribution. 
Then:
:$\var X = \dfrac {\alpha \beta} {\paren {\alpha + \beta}^2 \paren {\alpha + \beta + 1} }$

items.title: Variance of Binomial Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$.
Then the variance of $X$ is given by:
:$\var X = n p \paren {1 - p}$

items.title: Variance of Exponential Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$.
Then the variance of $X$ is:
:$\var X = \beta^2$

items.title: Variance of Gamma Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution.
The variance of $X$ is given by:
:$\var X = \dfrac \alpha {\beta^2}$

items.title: Variance of Geometric Distribution
Variance of Logistic Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which satisfies the logistic distribution:
:$X \sim \map {\operatorname {Logistic} } {\mu, s}$
The variance of $X$ is given by:
:$\var X = \dfrac {s^2 \pi^2} 3$

items.title: Variance of Normal Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X \sim N \paren {\mu, \sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution.
Then: 
:$\var X = \sigma^2$

items.title: Variance of Poisson Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$.
Then the variance of $X$ is given by:
:$\var X = \lambda$

items.title: Variance of Shifted Geometric Distribution
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the shifted geometric distribution with parameter $p$.
